  cover the selected export; speech may suggest boundaries, but silence never classifies automatic coding and
  unclassified time stays at 1×. Independent event markers, reviewed Auto-view scenes and validated video source
  coverage never change original media. Repository/branch association and an actual starting SHA precede reviewed
  time-to-SHA anchors; commit timestamps only propose positions after an explicit session/wall-clock calibration.
  Missing or rebased SHA references report unavailable. Manual edits persist across derived-track regeneration and
  appended takes; source revision changes are visible. Manifest schema 5 lists original and prepared workshop JSON
  sidecars clipped/rebased by the common IN/OUT recipe, retaining original coordinates and provenance. These files
  do not publish media or turn transcripts into participant subtitles.
- `/admin/shortener` manages public short links, QR/UTM output, destinations,
  notes, search/filter/sort state, and private click history. Links are served
  by `/[shortcode]`; `/shortener` redirects to the admin page.
- `/admin/login` authenticates the single `admin` account with `ADMIN_PASSWORD`
  and a signed session cookie. All `/admin/*` pages and APIs require
  `requireAdminSignedIn`. `/admin` is the post-login dashboard.
- Other public/legal routes include `/contact`, `/data-deletion`, `/privacy`,
  `/terms`, `/dekujeme`, `/branding`, and the routes under `/k`, `/old`, and
  `/test`.

#### Shared community and workshop behavior

- Workshop occurrences choose video, presentation, or their connected repository as the primary stage source. Old
  data defaults to video; the choice never changes which sources are stored. The countdown and wrap-up still follow
  `workshopPhase.ts`, and other readable sources remain supplementary special materials with recording access chosen
  by the server. Permanent room kinds which have no stage remain without one.

- Community and workshop participant rooms, including waiting rooms and community project views, share light,
  dark, and device appearance through `WorkshopRoomThemeProvider` and `workshopRoomTheme.css`. The browser remembers
  the choice across rooms and tabs; changing it preserves form and room state. Room palette tokens also reach
  portalled membership/project dialogs and cookie controls. Public landing pages and administration keep their own
  appearance.

- The global cookie banner shares its page palette with its settings dialog, uses
  a shallow bottom strip on desktop and an inset panel on phones, and reserves its
  measured height so the end of each page stays reachable. Fixed bottom controls
  such as the podcast player and admin table scrollbar opt into clearance through
  `data-fixed-bottom-control`; the banner, booking notice, and coder badge measure
  their neighbors through `hooks/useFixedControlClearance.ts`.

- Rooms lead to each other in both directions, through one identity hand-off. The
  community lists the terms and opens the room of each; an invited workshop room
  places its community link beside its materials as a special material for every
  participant, regardless of paid membership. Where a special material sits is
  decided once, in `lib/workshops/workshopSpecialMaterials.ts`: a card says where
  among the ordinary materials it belongs, and the invitation opens the material
  list of a participant who does not pay while it closes the list of a paying
  member. A membership which is not loaded yet leaves it where a participant who
  does not pay reads it. Both carry the connected member's
  name and email on, and an incomplete identity carries nothing rather than half
  of it. Which rooms invite is answered by
  `lib/workshops/workshopKindCapabilities.ts`; the community and project
  discussions do not. The invitation names the community's sections by the names
  the community itself uses.
- Community polls attached to workshops are shared. A normalized email gives a
  member one vote across the community and all attached workshops. An
  administrator can enable an Other answer: a member-written response becomes
  one shared, anonymous option and receives that member's vote atomically, so
  every room can vote for it; later poll edits keep member-written answers.
  Such an answer goes through the very moderation a chat message does, by the
  one shared submission policy in `lib/workshops/workshopSubmissionStatus.ts`:
  it is pending until the shared AI review or a moderator approves it, while a trusted member and a
  moderator have theirs approved as they write it. The vote of its writer is
  counted at once either way, but until the answer is approved only its writer
  and the moderators of the room owning the poll receive it or its vote, and a
  rejected answer is gone for everybody. Who may read one answer is decided
  once, in `lib/workshops/workshopPollOptionVisibility.ts`.
  Workshops may display and accept votes, but the community owns administration.
  Where a room puts its polls is decided once, in
  `lib/workshops/workshopPollPlacement.ts`: the community, which decides in its
  own polls, opens with them, while a workshop, which is only their subject,
  keeps them below the materials it was held for.
- The participant room owns the membership badge and popup. Community and live
  workshop rooms use the same membership for the connecting email, and checkout
  returns to the room where it started. Membership is offered only by room kinds
  listed in `lib/workshops/workshopKindCapabilities.ts`; project discussions do
  not offer it.
- Members can open Stripe Customer Portal from the popup. In-app cancellation
  stops only the next renewal, preserves access through the paid period, appears
  in the badge, and can be reversed before that period ends.
- A full-price-for-the-whole-term discount is a voucher: atomically consume it,
  create membership immediately, ask for no card, and create no Stripe renewal.
  A limited-month discount still opens checkout because the regular price returns.
  Stripe webhooks update completed, cancelled, failed, and late payments. With no
  Stripe key, hide membership; with test keys, identify the test payment gate.
- Community projects use a URL-first metadata wizard. Ordinary submissions await
  AI or manual moderation; trusted members and moderators are approved immediately. Pending
  projects remain visible to their author and moderators.
- A live workshop room has a countdown before it starts and, while it runs, the
  event's selected primary stage content: video, presentation, or the connected
  repository. Existing and unset choices mean video. Other configured sources
  stay in the shared special-material list, with recordings still selected by
  the server's member access rule. After the recorded end, the stage returns to
  the wrap-up. Permanent rooms such as the community do not gain a stage. The
  room also has reactions, watching count, moderated chat, timed materials, and
  attached poll aggregates. An open-ended term runs until its recorded end; its
  stage does not end automatically. Admins
  can select, replace, clear, or create the displayed comment through the same
  private realtime channel used by reactions.
- Workshop and community chat can use reusable Book agents, administered in their shared Agents tab with
  `BookEditor` from `@promptbook/components`. `LiteAgent` from `@promptbook/node` uses `OPENAI_API_KEY`; definitions
  are shared while replies, listening and cooldowns are enabled per room. Only newly approved comments enqueue
  replies, including artificial and other agent messages, with at most two agent turns. A durable database queue
  owns leases, deduplication and rechecks of moderation, agent settings and room state before publication.
  Public messages use the existing chat rendering; admin projections and exports distinguish `user`, `artificial`
  and `agent` origins with agent/run provenance. Agents have no participant sessions or membership access.
  Live questions require an administrator's active stream-tab or microphone capture in the Agents tab; audio is
  transcribed in short standalone segments and never saved. Private transcripts feed the agents only during an
  ongoing workshop and only from its current, unexpired capture session. Stopping capture or ending the workshop
  prevents its pending live questions from publishing; publication locks that session against a concurrent stop.
  Project rooms and externally organized events offer no agents. Persistent servers run the queue in the background;
  serverless hosts can use the authenticated scheduler route documented in `README.md`.
- A term can be about a project. The connection is one value — GitHub repository,
  the default branch, and one or more branch patterns such as `main`, `client-*`,
  `feature/*`, or `*` for all branches, plus any number of public deployment
  addresses, written one per line — so it is set, changed, and unset at once and
  neither branch selection nor deployment
  outlives its repository. Room kinds which offer it are named in
  `lib/workshops/workshopKindCapabilities.ts`. The room shows the repository as a
  special material beside its ordinary materials for every participant, with its
  links, every deployment and newest commits, marking those which arrive while a
  participant watches;
  a newly found commit is broadcast to active rooms and appears on the stage for
  ten seconds. A selection resolving to multiple branches is shown as a commit
  graph. Commits come from the public commit feed or keyless API, pooled once per
  server and cached through the revalidation window; an unreadable feed still
  leaves the room naming its project. A project deployed once is opened as the live
  application of the workshop; several deployments are each named by their own
  address, and the first of them is the one a term card and the participant project panel are previewed from.
  Both reuse the deployment's image, title and description through the shared project preview; missing metadata or
  a broken image keeps the deployment address visible, with repository-only previews reserved for undeployed projects.
  The participant preview opens that deployment and loads independently of room state and commits, through an
  authenticated endpoint using the stored project. Changing rooms, repositories or the primary deployment discards
  stale previews. Community term cards keep their workshop destination.
  With a repository and no deployment URL, administration offers direct Vercel deployment using private `VERCEL_TOKEN`
  and optional `VERCEL_TEAM_ID`. One Vercel project per repository stays connected to its original GitHub source and
  deploys its production branch (initially the default branch), independently of the workshop's history selection.
  Administration polls the build and fills in its assigned production alias only when ready; the ordinary settings
  save publishes that URL. Manual URLs, a changed repository, and switching rooms discard stale pending results.
  Deployment failures show the reported reason and code, targeted recovery steps, and an optional bounded build-log
  excerpt with credentials redacted. Canceled, blocked, and alias-assignment failures have distinct guidance; missing
  diagnostics keep fallback checks and the Vercel link available. Only authenticated administration receives them.
  This adds no workshop data fields; setup and retry behavior are documented in `README.md`.
  The connection can also carry independent starting and ending commit IDs. Administration previews each commit's
  message, author and Prague date, and can fill each bound separately from the workshop time (first commit at or after
  the start, last at or before the end). Bounds are inclusive by commit time across the selected branches. The room
  initially shows and highlights that range; expanding and paging its graph reveals history outside it while retaining
  the highlight. An omitted bound leaves that side open; two omitted bounds leave the history unfiltered. Every lookup,
  autofill and history page uses the same branch selection, and commits belonging only to other branches stay hidden.
- A workshop can carry one public presentation URL for a PDF, PowerPoint file, or
  GitHub Markdown page. The room renders it beside ordinary materials through the
  shared material card, primary action, preview card and flip-to-show QR code, for every participant without making
  it timed or membership-gated content.
- Paid-only materials are decided on the server in one pass. Members receive
  unlocked material; others receive only the published titles as an offer. An
  untitled item is not named, items are not named before their unlock time, and a
  room without membership hides paid-only items without naming them.
- After a workshop ends, its recording is server-gated to members. Others receive
  the published teaser, or a generic offer when no teaser exists; a term without
  a recording offers nothing. An administrator writes the recording's start
  offset as hours, minutes and seconds, while it stays stored, exported and read
  in seconds; it applies only to that paid replay and never to the countdown or
  live stream.
  A workshop can instead select a hosted synchronized recording while preserving its inactive YouTube settings.
  Direct admin import and studio publication use the same private multipart object storage and schema 5 validation;
  verified revisions publish atomically, and old revisions remain briefly for connected viewers. Room JSON and every
  hosted manifest/range request apply the same live/free and paid replay rule. Prepared hosted media uses export zero,
  with recorded pause gaps mapped to the chosen live wall clock; the YouTube offset is never applied again. Imported
  subtitle sidecars stay out of the participant player. Cleanup claims inactive revisions before removing objects.
  The hosted participant player uses one prepared-export clock across Auto, Editor, Aplikace and Kamera, with a camera
  overlay in Auto, reviewed activity speed boundaries, event markers and anchored commit selection in the existing
  repository graph. Auto speed advances automatic-coding intervals through decoded steps at up to 10× and waits when
  decoding is slower. Free live playback serves only the completed, at-most-two-second segment at the server-delayed playhead through a
  time-authorized route; direct full-file bytes and other segments are denied. Members may seek the full published
  recording. Complete publication is required before this scheduled live delivery; it is not an ingest stream.
- Pending chat messages, member-written poll answers, and community projects use
  `lib/workshops/workshopAutoApproval.ts` for optional AI approval after saving.
  `WORKSHOP_AUTO_APPROVAL_API_KEY` enables it; the model and HTTPS base URL are
  configurable. Only clearly suitable content is approved; uncertainty, missing
  configuration, invalid output, and an eight-second timeout leave it pending.
  The database approves only unchanged pending content from a currently unbanned
  author and privately records the item, model, and time. AI never rejects, edits,
  grants trust, or replaces a human decision. It reviews text and URL metadata,
  without fetching linked pages or preview images. Moderator-created materials
  require no review, and old pending submissions are not bulk-processed.
- Trusted participants remain invisible and their messages are auto-approved.
  The participant lists in workshop and community administration show three exclusive, complete room counts:
  moderators, trusted non-moderators, and untrusted non-moderators. Their explicit bulk-trust action confirms a
  server-reviewed eligible set and updates that room atomically; a changed set requires a fresh confirmation.
  The separate automatic-trust setting defaults off for every new or duplicated room and is applied only when a new
  participant identity is inserted. Reconnects and later setting changes never rewrite an existing trust decision.
  Granting trust or moderator status also approves every pending submission by that room-local participant — chat,
  member-written poll answers, and community projects — in the same database transaction. Rejected items stay
  rejected; a ban blocks this approval until it is lifted. The private pending-submission view supplies both this
  approval and the complete per-person counts in room moderation and administrative participant lists. Community
  project cards refresh with the room without resetting the submission form.
  Moderators see pending messages, can approve/reject/correct/pin them, and can
  trust or silence authors. An administrator in `/admin/workshops` and a moderator
  in a workshop room can also turn any comment into an ordinary, immediately
  available material. That preserves the comment in chat, carries its complete
  Markdown body into the material, and names its author in the material title;
  both entry points use the shared material creation path, including its short
  links and room refresh. Workshop and community moderators are appointed in
  `/admin/workshops`; project authors moderate their own discussions.
- The room records whether each open browser is actively or passively attended
  from pointer, typing, scroll, and touch activity. Admin analytics distinguish
  active computer users from merely open tabs with dashed audience lines.
- The community's compact gallery shows its five highest-upvoted approved projects
  and links to the full gallery. Community landing content is read from the live
  room: expose only anonymous totals, approved messages, and shared projects;
  show member first names only. If the room cannot be read, show less content,
  not an error. Landing-page reactions are estimates based on recent room data.

#### Administration and data rules

- Workshop and community settings render their shared `WorkshopSettingsForm` directly in the Settings tab,
  with autosave and navigation protection. Other admin creation and editing use the shared `AdminEditorDialog`
  (and `AdminEditorButton` for a local trigger).
  Lists show summaries and edit actions; contact notes and contacted status are edited in the contact dialog.
  The dialog contains request errors, traps and restores focus, and scrolls within the viewport. Closing with its
  button or Escape flushes pending saves and keeps invalid or failed drafts open; backdrop clicks preserve the editor.
  Search, filters, and immediate moderation actions stay in their lists. New records still require explicit creation.

- Existing records in `/admin` autosave through `useAdminAutosave` and the shared `AdminSaveQueue`.
  Raw drafts remain dirty through validation failures and failed requests; writes are debounced and serialized,
  and polling must not replace an editor's draft. Editors stay open after autosave. Pending writes protect
  close/reload with the browser's native warning; admin links, section/record switches, and sign-out flush saves
  before leaving. Explicit API mutations share `requestAdminJson`/`protectAdminMutation` for in-flight protection.
  Creation and destructive actions remain explicit. Keep record editors keyed by their stable database identity.
  Immediate material unlocking shares its draft save. Poll updates return generated prepared-choice IDs; the editor
  carries them into subsequent saves while preserving newer text, so autosaving never recreates a saved choice.

- Event kinds are defined once in `lib/events/eventTypes.ts`; adding one should
  not require database migration or page-specific duplication. Terms ask for kind,
  online/place format, price, and capacity. Each kind also names where its landing
  page records registrations, which is the `placeName` of the contacts it gathers.
  A kind which names no landing page is held by somebody else: its terms carry the
  address they are held at, are refused without one, and this application runs no
  room, gathers no registration, and returns no payer to them.
- Which term a registration belongs to is decided once, in
  `lib/workshops/workshopRegistrations.ts`. A term is recognised by its slug, by
  its Prague day, and by the moment it begins at, so registrations written before
  terms had slugs keep counting. Registration forms write the term through the
  same line prefixes that rule reads back. Contacts are still gathered, recorded
  and shown only by `/admin/contacts`; counting reads nothing but their notes.
  The registration actions in workshop administration carry that same term filter
  into the contacts list and its exports.
- Workshop polls are read-only in workshop administration, except for the
  answers members wrote into them: an administrator approves, rejects, rewords,
  or deletes one together with the votes cast for it, and reads it named by the
  author who wrote it, while a moderator of the room owning the poll only
  decides about it from the room itself. Creating a new event
  publishes it by default; duplicating an event keeps it published unless the
  source is unpublished. Duplicating a workshop preserves its connections to
  the already existing attached polls; it creates no polls, options, votes, or room history. Stage settings contain
  the live stream, paid-recording start offset, and recording teaser; presentation settings the public presentation
  address, and project settings the repository the term is about, written as an
  address or as `owner/name`, together with its branch patterns. Deleting a workshop is a soft deletion: its room
  data and attached
  community polls stay stored, but the term leaves normal public and administrative
  lists and no longer holds its slug for a replacement. An end may be empty;
  admins can record, adjust, clear, and reopen it. Overview analytics are zoomable and share their
  room, section, lines, reaction, zoom, and keyword metrics through query params.
- Community administration is the workshop dashboard restricted to the
  `community` room kind: no room picker, schedule, stage, reactions, or address.
  Its membership view filters Stripe lifecycle, prices, discounts, identifiers,
  dates, test/live mode, and links to the exact Stripe checkout/subscription.
  Community analytics cover all measured time and member details show seen times.
- Shortener search, provenance filters, sorting, and selected click history live
  in GET parameters. Editing changes only shortcode, destinations, note, and
  landing page; deletion also deletes recorded clicks.

#### Database and verification

- Put database changes in `migrations/*.sql`. Startup and
  `npm run migrate-database` run `_initialize.sql`, then migrations in filename
  order, recording immutable filenames and checksums in `public."Migration"`.
  Changed or missing migrations fail, as do queries requiring an unapplied one.
- `npm run test-types` must build before `tsc` to refresh `.next/types`.
- `npm run test-e2e` uses the Next.js development server; first-request compile
  headroom belongs in `playwright.config.ts`, not individual tests. E2E tests are
  independent and retry once in a fresh browser context for transient failures;
  failed-attempt traces remain available. Each attempt archives one recording in
  `tests/e2e/videos/`, retaining only recent runs.
- Recording-studio E2E sources use canvas video and synthesized audio with a silent Web Audio output, independent
  of physical audio-device clocks. Keep recording, storage, codecs, trimming, and ZIP exports real in these tests.
  Recorded A/V markers are checked from decoded sample timestamps rather than speaker-output latency. The preparation
  fixture additionally carries readable/binary timecodes and claps at 25/30 fps with distinct startup offsets.
  Simulated ten-hour mappings and decoder delays do not establish a ten-hour capture soak or physical macOS behavior.

createSitemapLanguageAlternates(definition: PageMetadataDefinition): Record<string, string> | undefined {\n    if (!definition.languageAlternates) {\n        return undefined;\n    }\n\n    return {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01REVs16sZ6kRst93VamnmZW","type":"tool_result","content":"1\timport type { PageMetadataDefinition } from '@/lib/metadata/page-metadata-definition';\n2\timport { createAbsoluteUrl, SITE_NAME } from '@/lib/metadata/site-config';\n3\timport type { SocialPreviewBrandKind } from '@/lib/metadata/social-preview-assets';\n4\timport type { SocialPreviewArtworkKind } from '@/lib/metadata/social-preview-artwork';\n5\timport type { SocialPreviewImageOptions } from '@/lib/metadata/social-preview-image';\n6\timport {\n7\t    createSocialPreviewPalette,\n8\t    PROMPTBOOK_SOCIAL_PREVIEW_PALETTE,\n9\t    type SocialPreviewPaletteSeed,\n10\t} from '@/lib/metadata/social-preview-palette';\n11\t\n12\t/**\n13\t * Page specific part of a sharing preview image\n14\t *\n15\t * Note: The headline is intentionally missing here - it is taken from the\n16\t *       page definition so that a sharing preview can never drift away from\n17\t *       what the page actually claims. The remaining configuration is visual,\n18\t *       not a second set of marketing copy.\n19\t */\n20\texport type SocialPreviewContent = {\n21\t    /**\n22\t     * Small uppercase line above the headline\n23\t     */\n24\t    readonly eyebrow: string;\n25\t\n26\t    /**\n27\t     * Non-textual visual metaphor matched to what the page is about\n28\t     */\n29\t    readonly artwork: SocialPreviewArtworkKind;\n30\t\n31\t    /**\n32\t     * Colors specific to the page\n33\t     */\n34\t    readonly paletteSeed: SocialPreviewPaletteSeed;\n35\t\n36\t    /**\n37\t     * Brand shown next to its mark, defaults to the page's brand or the site name\n38\t     */\n39\t    readonly brandLabel?: string;\n40\t\n41\t    /** The local brand mark and, for a personal page, its portrait. */\n42\t    readonly brandKind?: SocialPreviewBrandKind;\n43\t};\n44\t\n45\t/**\n46\t * Combines a page definition with its page specific artwork into complete sharing preview image options\n47\t *\n48\t * @param definition single source of truth describing the page\n49\t * @param content page specific part of the sharing preview\n50\t */\n51\texport function createSocialPreviewOptions(\n52\t    definition: PageMetadataDefinition,\n53\t    content: Partial<SocialPreviewContent> = {},\n54\t): SocialPreviewImageOptions {\n55\t    const socialTitle = definition.socialTitle ?? definition.title;\n56\t\n57\t    return {\n58\t        alt: definition.socialPreviewImageAlt ?? socialTitle,\n59\t        brandLabel: content.brandLabel ?? definition.brand?.name ?? SITE_NAME,\n60\t        brandKind: content.brandKind ?? 'promptbook',\n61\t        eyebrow:\n62\t            content.eyebrow ??\n63\t            (definition.language === 'cs' ? 'Informace a užitečné odkazy' : 'Information & resources'),\n64\t        title: socialTitle,\n65\t        description: definition.socialDescription ?? definition.description,\n66\t        hostname: new URL(createAbsoluteUrl(definition.path)).hostname,\n67\t        artwork: content.artwork ?? 'knowledge',\n68\t        palette: createSocialPreviewPalette(content.paletteSeed ?? PROMPTBOOK_SOCIAL_PREVIEW_PALETTE),\n69\t    };\n70\t}\n71\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"e45c8504-6a06-43dd-b769-a6ab7d0996f1","uuid":"d8fd010c-62e7-40f5-b58d-f09590cfbcac","timestamp":"2026-09-30T21:59:03.284Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\me\\work\\promptbook-experiments-and-landing-pages\\aldaron\\lib\\metadata\\create-social-preview-options.ts","content":"import type { PageMetadataDefinition } from '@/lib/metadata/page-metadata-definition';\nimport { createAbsoluteUrl, SITE_NAME } from '@/lib/metadata/site-config';\nimport type { SocialPreviewBrandKind } from '@/lib/metadata/social-preview-assets';\nimport type { SocialPreviewArtworkKind } from '@/lib/metadata/social-preview-artwork';\nimport type { SocialPreviewImageOptions } from '@/lib/metadata/social-preview-image';\nimport {\n    createSocialPreviewPalette,\n    PROMPTBOOK_SOCIAL_PREVIEW_PALETTE,\n    type SocialPreviewPaletteSeed,\n} from '@/lib/metadata/social-preview-palette';\n\n/**\n * Page specific part of a sharing preview image\n *\n * Note: The headline is intentionally missing here - it is taken from the\n *       page definition so that a sharing preview can never drift away from\n *       what the page actually claims. The remaining configuration is visual,\n *       not a second set of marketing copy.\n */\nexport type SocialPreviewContent = {\n    /**\n     * Small uppercase line above the headline\n     */\n    readonly eyebrow: string;\n\n    /**\n     * Non-textual visual metaphor matched to what the page is about\n     */\n    readonly artwork: SocialPreviewArtworkKind;\n\n    /**\n     * Colors specific to the page\n     */\n    readonly paletteSeed: SocialPreviewPaletteSeed;\n\n    /**\n     * Brand shown next to its mark, defaults to the page's brand or the site name\n     */\n    readonly brandLabel?: string;\n\n    /** The local brand mark and, for a personal page, its portrait. */\n    readonly brandKind?: SocialPreviewBrandKind;\n};\n\n/**\n * Combines a page definition with its page specific artwork into complete sharing preview image options\n *\n * @param definition single source of truth describing the page\n * @param content page specific part of the sharing preview\n */\nexport function createSocialPreviewOptions(\n    definition: PageMetadataDefinition,\n    content: Partial<SocialPreviewContent> = {},\n): SocialPreviewImageOptions {\n    const socialTitle = definition.socialTitle ?? definition.title;\n\n    return {\n        alt: definition.socialPreviewImageAlt ?? socialTitle,\n        brandLabel: content.brandLabel ?? definition.brand?.name ?? SITE_NAME,\n        brandKind: content.brandKind ?? 'promptbook',\n        eyebrow:\n            content.eyebrow ??\n            (definition.language === 'cs' ? 'Informace a užitečné odkazy' : 'Information & resources'),\n        title: socialTitle,\n        description: definition.socialDescription ?? definition.description,\n        hostname: new URL(createAbsoluteUrl(definition.path)).hostname,\n        artwork: content.artwork ?? 'knowledge',\n        palette: createSocialPreviewPalette(content.paletteSeed ?? PROMPTBOOK_SOCIAL_PREVIEW_PALETTE),\n    };\n}\n","numLines":71,"startLine":1,"totalLines":71}}}

createPublicDomainRedirectResponse(request: NextRequest, publicDomainRoute: PublicDomainRoute) {\n    const redirectUrl = new URL(getPublicPathname(publicDomainRoute, request.nextUrl.pathname), publicDomainRoute.origin);\n    redirectUrl.search = request.nextUrl.search;\n\n    return NextResponse.redirect(redirectUrl, 308);\n}\n\nexport function middleware(request: NextRequest) {\n    const requestHostname = getPublicRequestHostname(request.headers, request.nextUrl.hostname);\n    const publicDomainRoute = getPublicDomainRouteByHostname(requestHostname);\n\n    // A custom domain keeps its concise public path in the address bar while Next renders the existing nested route.\n    if (publicDomainRoute) {\n        if (request.nextUrl.pathname === '/robots.txt') {\n            return new NextResponse(createPublicDomainRobotsText(publicDomainRoute), {\n                headers: { 'Content-Type': 'text/plain; charset=utf-8' },\n            });\n        }\n\n        if (request.nextUrl.pathname === '/sitemap.xml') {\n            return new NextResponse(createPublicDomainSitemapXml(publicDomainRoute), {\n                headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/xml; charset=utf-8' },\n            });\n        }\n\n        const internalPathname = getInternalPathname(publicDomainRoute, request.nextUrl.pathname);\n\n        if (internalPathname) {\n            const rewriteUrl = request.nextUrl.clone();\n            rewriteUrl.pathname = internalPathname;\n\n            return NextResponse.rewrite(rewriteUrl);\n        }\n\n        const legacyDomainRoute = getPublicDomainRouteByInternalPathname(request.nextUrl.pathname);\n\n        // Old nested links to this same site normalize to its public path. An old path owned by a different site\n        // must never become a cross-site redirect when requested on this domain.\n        if (legacyDomainRoute?.hostname === publicDomainRoute.hostname) {\n            return createPublicDomainRedirectResponse(request, publicDomainRoute);\n        }\n\n        if (isSharedDeploymentAssetPath(request.nextUrl.pathname)) {\n            return NextResponse.next();\n        }\n\n        return new NextResponse(createPublicDomainNotFoundHtml(publicDomainRoute), {\n            status: 404,\n            headers: {\n                'Content-Type': 'text/html; charset=utf-8',\n                'Cache-Control': 'no-store',\n                'X-Robots-Tag': 'noindex, nofollow',\n            },\n        });\n    }\n\n    if (isPrimarySiteHostname(requestHostname)) {\n        const legacyDomainRoute = getPublicDomainRouteByInternalPathname(request.nextUrl.pathname);\n\n        if (legacyDomainRoute) {\n            return createPublicDomainRedirectResponse(request, legacyDomainRoute);\n        }\n    }\n\n    if (request.nextUrl.pathname === '/pavol') {\n        const language = getPreferredHomepageLanguage(request.headers.get('accept-language'));\n        const redirectUrl = request.nextUrl.clone();\n        redirectUrl.pathname = `/${language}/pavol`;\n\n        return NextResponse.redirect(redirectUrl);\n    }\n\n    if (request.nextUrl.pathname !== '/') {\n        return NextResponse.next();\n    }\n\n    const language = getPreferredHomepageLanguage(request.headers.get('accept-language'));\n    const redirectUrl = request.nextUrl.clone();\n\n    redirectUrl.pathname = `/${language}`;\n\n    return NextResponse.redirect(redirectUrl);\n}\n\nexport const config = {\n    matcher: ['/((?!api|_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico).*)'],\n};\n","numLines":106,"startLine":1,"totalLines":106}}}

{isSubmitted ? Isolating every route keeps earlier cold compilations\n    // from exhausting the timeout of a healthy page later in the smoke suite.\n    test(`public landing and information page loads: ${path}`, async ({ page }) => {\n        await expectPublicPageToLoad(page, path);\n    });\n}\n\ntest('AI ta Krajta collaboration section deep-links to its media kit', async ({ page }) => {\n    await page.goto(AI_TA_KRAJTA_PATH, { waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded' });\n\n    const mediaKitLink = page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Otevřít media kit' });\n    await expect(mediaKitLink).toHaveAttribute('href', AI_TA_KRAJTA_MEDIA_KIT_PATH);\n    await mediaKitLink.click();\n\n    await expect(page).toHaveURL(AI_TA_KRAJTA_MEDIA_KIT_PATH);\n    await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /Oslovte české a slovenské publikum/i })).toBeVisible();\n});\n\ntest('AI ta Krajta owns its metadata, icon and installable manifest and credits Promptbook coder', async ({ page }) => {\n    await page.goto(AI_TA_KRAJTA_PATH, { waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded' });\n    await expect(page.locator('footer')).toBeVisible();\n    await expect(page).toHaveTitle(`${AI_TA_KRAJTA_BRAND_NAME} | Český podcast o umělé inteligenci`);\n\n    const metadataIdentity = await page.evaluate(\n        ({ scalableIconPath, rasterIconPath, manifestPath, rssFeedMediaType, rssFeedUrl, rssFeedLabel }) => {\n            const identityTags = Array.from(document.head.querySelectorAll('meta, link'));\n            const structuredDataNodes = Array.from(document.head.querySelectorAll('script[type*=ld]'));\n            const footerText = document.querySelector('footer')?.textContent ?? '';\n\n            const isPromptbookIdentityAbsent = identityTags\n                .filter((element) => /application-name|creator|publisher|og:site_name|twitter:site/.test(element.outerHTML))\n                .every((element) => !element.outerHTML.includes('Promptbook'));\n            const isPromptbookStructuredDataAbsent = structuredDataNodes.every(\n                (element) => !(element.textContent ?? '').includes('Promptbook'),\n            );\n            const isPodcastIconUsed = identityTags.some(\n                (element) =>\n                    element.getAttribute('rel') === 'icon' && element.getAttribute('href') === scalableIconPath,\n            );\n            const isPodcastTouchIconUsed = identityTags.some(\n                (element) =>\n                    element.getAttribute('rel') === 'apple-touch-icon' &&\n                    element.getAttribute('href') === rasterIconPath,\n            );\n            const isPodcastManifestUsed = identityTags.some(\n                (element) => element.getAttribute('rel') === 'manifest' && element.getAttribute('href') === manifestPath,\n            );\n            const isPodcastRssFeedAdvertised = identityTags.some(\n                (element) =>\n                    element.getAttribute('rel') === 'alternate' &&\n                    element.getAttribute('type') === rssFeedMediaType &&\n                    element.getAttribute('href') === rssFeedUrl,\n            );\n            const isPodcastRssFeedLinked = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('a')).some(\n                (element) => element.textContent?.trim() === rssFeedLabel && element.getAttribute('href') === rssFeedUrl,\n            );\n            const isLegalCompanyPresent = footerText.includes('AI Web s.r.o.');\n\n            return {\n                isPromptbookIdentityAbsent,\n                isPromptbookStructuredDataAbsent,\n                isPodcastIconUsed,\n                isPodcastTouchIconUsed,\n                isPodcastManifestUsed,\n                isPodcastRssFeedAdvertised,\n                isPodcastRssFeedLinked,\n                isLegalCompanyPresent,\n            };\n        },\n        {\n            scalableIconPath: AI_TA_KRAJTA_APP_ICONS.SCALABLE.path,\n            rasterIconPath: AI_TA_KRAJTA_APP_ICONS.RASTER.path,\n            manifestPath: AI_TA_KRAJTA_MANIFEST_PATH,\n            rssFeedMediaType: AI_TA_KRAJTA_RSS_FEED_MEDIA_TYPE,\n            rssFeedUrl: AI_TA_KRAJTA_RSS_FEED_PLATFORM.url,\n            rssFeedLabel: AI_TA_KRAJTA_RSS_FEED_PLATFORM.label,\n        },\n    );\n\n    expect(metadataIdentity).toEqual({\n        isPromptbookIdentityAbsent: true,\n        isPromptbookStructuredDataAbsent: true,\n        isPodcastIconUsed: true,\n        isPodcastTouchIconUsed: true,\n        isPodcastManifestUsed: true,\n        isPodcastRssFeedAdvertised: true,\n        isPodcastRssFeedLinked: true,\n        isLegalCompanyPresent: true,\n    });\n\n    await expect(page.locator('footer').getByRole('link', { name: 'Done by Promptbook coder', exact: true }))\n        .toHaveAttribute('href', 'https://coder.ptbk.io/');\n\n    const manifestResponse = await page.request.get(AI_TA_KRAJTA_MANIFEST_PATH);\n\n    expect(manifestResponse.ok()).toBeTruthy();\n    expect(await manifestResponse.json()).toMatchObject({\n        name: AI_TA_KRAJTA_BRAND_NAME,\n        short_name: AI_TA_KRAJTA_BRAND_NAME,\n        icons: [\n            { src: AI_TA_KRAJTA_APP_ICONS.SCALABLE.path, purpose: 'any' },\n            { src: AI_TA_KRAJTA_APP_ICONS.RASTER.path, purpose: 'any' },\n            { src: AI_TA_KRAJTA_APP_ICONS.RASTER.path, purpose: 'maskable' },\n        ],\n    });\n\n    for (const appIcon of [AI_TA_KRAJTA_APP_ICONS.SCALABLE, AI_TA_KRAJTA_APP_ICONS.RASTER]) {\n        const iconResponse = await page.request.get(appIcon.path);\n\n        expect(iconResponse.ok(), `Expected ${appIcon.path} to be served`).toBeTruthy();\n        expect(iconResponse.headers()['content-type']).toContain(appIcon.type);\n    }\n});\n\ntest('AI ta Krajta searches complete transcripts on the server without sending them to the browser', async ({ page, request }) => {\n    const transcriptSearchResponse = await request.get(\n        `${AI_TA_KRAJTA_EPISODE_SEARCH_API_PATH}?${new URLSearchParams({ search: 'zahradníkem' }).toString()}`,\n    );\n    const transcriptSearchResponseText = await transcriptSearchResponse.text();\n\n    expect(transcriptSearchResponse.ok()).toBeTruthy();\n    expect(JSON.parse(transcriptSearchResponseText)).toMatchObject({ episodeSlugs: expect.arrayContaining(['65']) });\n    expect(transcriptSearchResponseText).not.toContain('Kozel za hradníkem');\n\n    await page.goto(AI_TA_KRAJTA_PATH, { waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded' });\n    await page.getByRole('searchbox', { name: 'Hledat v dílech' }).fill('zahradníkem');\n\n    await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /AI zrychlí vývoj 10x/ })).toBeVisible();\n    await expect(page.locator('body')).not.toContainText('Kozel za hradníkem');\n});\n\nfor (const publicRedirect of PUBLIC_REDIRECTS) {\n    test(`public address redirects to its page: ${publicRedirect.path}`, async ({ request }) => {\n        test.setTimeout(PUBLIC_PAGE_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS);\n\n        const destinationPath = await readRedirectDestination(request, publicRedirect.path, publicRedirect.statusCode);\n\n        expect(\n            publicRedirect.destinationPaths.some((candidatePath) => candidatePath === destinationPath),\n            `Expected ${publicRedirect.path} to redirect to ${publicRedirect.destinationPaths.join(\n                ' or ',\n            )}, but it pointed at ${destinationPath}`,\n        ).toBeTruthy();\n    });\n}\n\ntest(`${RETIRED_TRAINING_PATH} carries a discount code to the workshop registration`, async ({ request }) => {\n    test.setTimeout(PUBLIC_PAGE_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS);\n\n    const destinationPath = await readRedirectDestination(\n        request,\n        `${RETIRED_TRAINING_PATH}?${DISCOUNT_CODE_QUERY_PARAMETER}=${encodeURIComponent(E2E_DISCOUNT_CODE)}`,\n        PERMANENT_REDIRECT_STATUS_CODE,\n    );\n\n    expect(destinationPath, `Expected ${RETIRED_TRAINING_PATH} to pre-fill the discount code it was given`).toBe(\n        createDiscountCodePrefillPath(AI_SUPERVIZE_MINI_PATH, REGISTRATION_SECTION_ID, E2E_DISCOUNT_CODE),\n    );\n});\n","numLines":291,"startLine":1,"totalLines":291}}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01HUNcZ6T8s4CKPLS4aLL83a","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t[ ]\n2\t\n3\t[✨⚙️] Reposition the main Promptbook homepage around autonomous agendas\n4\t\n5\t- Replace the **main Promptbook homepage proposition** with the product model described below. This is a conceptual repositioning, not a cosmetic copy refresh.\n6\t- Prerequisite/context: the previous PRD preserves today's Czech company-data landing page at `/cs/pro-firmy`. Do not delete that proposition while redesigning the main homepage.\n7\t- The central mental model must change from **\"AI agent / virtual employee that answers questions over documents\"** to **\"Promptbook turns powerful AI agents into long-running agendas/responsibilities that operate in the background.\"**\n8\t- Core idea to communicate:\n9\t    - Modern coding agents/harnesses can already perform remarkably complex one-shot tasks.\n10\t    - A company or project does not primarily need more impressive one-shot prompts. It needs important responsibilities to be handled reliably over time.\n11\t    - Promptbook packages those responsibilities as an **agenda**: a bounded area of responsibility with its own context, goals, recurring and one-off tasks, agents, rules and tools.\n12\t    - Multiple agents can work inside one agenda. The agenda is the durable unit; an individual agent or prompt is an implementation detail.\n13\t    - The agenda should be able to keep running in the background instead of requiring a human to repeatedly open a chat, restate context and ask for the next action.\n14\t    - Human interaction still matters: people can inspect, correct, approve, steer and change the agenda. The promise is not \"humans disappear\"; it is that routine continuation does not require continuous prompting.\n15\t- A useful framing is: **companies are made of agendas / responsibilities, not prompts**. A healthy company resembles a well-running machine because its recurring responsibilities keep being handled. Promptbook should make more of those responsibilities executable by AI.\n16\t- Avoid presenting \"agenda\" as merely a synonym for a scheduled task. An agenda can contain many goals and many tasks with different lifecycles. For example, accounting is an agenda; VAT filing, deadline monitoring and document processing are tasks/goals within it.\n17\t- Examples are important for comprehension, but the homepage must not make Promptbook look like a single-purpose accounting, inbox or website product. Use examples to reveal the general principle, then return to the abstraction.\n18\t- Strong example to feature: **a website/application that maintains itself**.\n19\t    - One-shot website/app generators can create an impressive initial result, but a real website or application needs ongoing maintenance and evolution.\n20\t    - Promptbook can use strong coding harnesses to turn \"maintain and evolve this application\" into an ongoing agenda: understand the repository, work through changes, maintain quality, test, fix, update and continue over time.\n21\t    - The user should perceive the maintained product/responsibility, not be forced to operate the underlying coding harness manually.\n22\t- Other illustrative agendas can include customer communication / keeping an inbox handled, accounting/administrative responsibilities, content or website operations, and company-specific operational responsibilities. Keep examples credible and avoid claiming unsupported fully autonomous/legal/accounting capabilities as already guaranteed.\n23\t- Product differentiation to communicate without turning the hero into a technical feature list:\n24\t    - **Professional/project context:** designed for real company/project responsibilities, not only personal background automations.\n25\t    - **Vendor independence:** the durable agenda is not conceptually tied to one model vendor. Promptbook can orchestrate different capable models/coding harnesses (for example OpenAI Codex, Claude Code and OpenCode) as implementation choices. Verify the exact supported integrations in the repository/product before making named compatibility claims.\n26\t    - **Coding harnesses as leverage:** Promptbook deliberately builds on very strong coding agents/harnesses. Code can exist under the hood when it is the best way to execute an agenda, without exposing that complexity as the user's primary interface.\n27\t    - **Git/repository as durable workspace:** where appropriate, explain that an agenda can live in a folder/Git repository containing durable context, agent definitions, instructions/PRDs/tasks and history. Do not require a nontechnical visitor to understand Git before they understand the product.\n28\t- Messaging hierarchy:\n29\t    1. First make the visitor understand the outcome: **a responsibility can keep being handled in the background**.\n30\t    2. Then introduce the word **agenda** and explain it as a durable area of responsibility.\n31\t    3. Show how an agenda contains context + goals/tasks + agents/tools and persists over time.\n32\t    4. Show concrete examples, with self-maintaining software/web as the strongest/most native example.\n33\t    5. Only after the concept is clear explain the technical leverage: strong coding harnesses, repositories, multiple models/vendors.\n34\t- The page must clearly contrast:\n35\t    - **one-shot AI:** \"do this task now\" / impressive but ends after the task,\n36\t    - **agenda:** \"take responsibility for this area over time\" / continues, observes, acts and escalates when needed.\n37\t- Do not frame ChatGPT, Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode or other strong agents as bad or obsolete. The positioning is explicitly that these systems are excellent and Promptbook **builds on their strength** to make them persistent and operational.\n38\t- Avoid generic AI-marketing language such as \"revolutionize your business\", \"AI employee for everything\", or unsupported claims of total autonomy.\n39\t- Avoid over-indexing on the term \"agent\". A visitor should leave remembering **their agenda/responsibility**, not Promptbook's internal agent taxonomy.\n40\t- Avoid automatically adding supporting copy, subheadlines or explanatory filler under every heading. If text does not add new information, omit it. The heading and UI/visual itself should carry the idea whenever possible.\n41\t- Design direction:\n42\t    - Reuse the existing Promptbook visual language where it helps, but redesign sections whose current structure is coupled to the old company-document proposition.\n43\t    - Prefer a visual explanation of the model over walls of prose.\n44\t    - Consider a simple diagram/interactive composition such as `Agenda → context + tasks/goals + agents/tools → continuous background work → outcomes/escalations`, but implement the clearest solution consistent with the current design system.\n45\t    - Make \"one-shot → ongoing agenda\" visually obvious above the fold or immediately after the hero.\n46\t    - The page must remain polished and understandable on mobile, not only desktop.\n47\t- Information architecture:\n48\t    - `/cs` becomes the new Czech agenda-based main homepage.\n49\t    - `/en` should express the same product positioning in natural English, not a literal awkward translation. Use \"agenda\", \"area of responsibility\", \"ongoing responsibility\" or another clear formulation as needed, while preserving the product concept.\n50\t    - Root language redirect behavior in `app/page.tsx` must continue to work.\n51\t    - Update homepage metadata, descriptions, keywords, Open Graph/social preview copy/artwork and structured SEO data so they no longer describe the main product only as company-document Q&A.\n52\t    - Keep the preserved Czech company-focused/data-focused proposition accessible at `/cs/pro-firmy`.\n53\t- Conversion:\n54\t    - Keep a clear primary CTA, but make its surrounding copy fit the new proposition.\n55\t    - Inspect the current strategic-call/qualification flow and reuse it if it still makes sense. Do not silently break lead capture.\n56\t    - Do not manufacture scarcity, metrics, testimonials, customer claims, security claims or capabilities that are not supported by the current product/content.\n57\t- Existing content:\n58\t    - Audit `businesses/homepage/homepageContent.tsx` rather than mechanically rewriting strings in place. This is a conceptual repositioning, not a cosmetic copy refresh.\n- Prerequisite/context: the previous PRD preserves today's Czech company-data landing page at `/cs/pro-firmy`. Do not delete that proposition while redesigning the main homepage.\n- The central mental model must change from **\"AI agent / virtual employee that answers questions over documents\"** to **\"Promptbook turns powerful AI agents into long-running agendas/responsibilities that operate in the background.\"**\n- Core idea to communicate:\n    - Modern coding agents/harnesses can already perform remarkably complex one-shot tasks.\n    - A company or project does not primarily need more impressive one-shot prompts. It needs important responsibilities to be handled reliably over time.\n    - Promptbook packages those responsibilities as an **agenda**: a bounded area of responsibility with its own context, goals, recurring and one-off tasks, agents, rules and tools.\n    - Multiple agents can work inside one agenda. The agenda is the durable unit; an individual agent or prompt is an implementation detail.\n    - The agenda should be able to keep running in the background instead of requiring a human to repeatedly open a chat, restate context and ask for the next action.\n    - Human interaction still matters: people can inspect, correct, approve, steer and change the agenda. The promise is not \"humans disappear\"; it is that routine continuation does not require continuous prompting.\n- A useful framing is: **companies are made of agendas / responsibilities, not prompts**. A healthy company resembles a well-running machine because its recurring responsibilities keep being handled. Promptbook should make more of those responsibilities executable by AI.\n- Avoid presenting \"agenda\" as merely a synonym for a scheduled task. An agenda can contain many goals and many tasks with different lifecycles. For example, accounting is an agenda; VAT filing, deadline monitoring and document processing are tasks/goals within it.\n- Examples are important for comprehension, but the homepage must not make Promptbook look like a single-purpose accounting, inbox or website product. Use examples to reveal the general principle, then return to the abstraction.\n- Strong example to feature: **a website/application that maintains itself**.\n    - One-shot website/app generators can create an impressive initial result, but a real website or application needs ongoing maintenance and evolution.\n    - Promptbook can use strong coding harnesses to turn \"maintain and evolve this application\" into an ongoing agenda: understand the repository, work through changes, maintain quality, test, fix, update and continue over time.\n    - The user should perceive the maintained product/responsibility, not be forced to operate the underlying coding harness manually.\n- Other illustrative agendas can include customer communication / keeping an inbox handled, accounting/administrative responsibilities, content or website operations, and company-specific operational responsibilities. Keep examples credible and avoid claiming unsupported fully autonomous/legal/accounting capabilities as already guaranteed.\n- Product differentiation to communicate without turning the hero into a technical feature list:\n    - **Professional/project context:** designed for real company/project responsibilities, not only personal background automations.\n    - **Vendor independence:** the durable agenda is not conceptually tied to one model vendor. Promptbook can orchestrate different capable models/coding harnesses (for example OpenAI Codex, Claude Code and OpenCode) as implementation choices. Verify the exact supported integrations in the repository/product before making named compatibility claims.\n    - **Coding harnesses as leverage:** Promptbook deliberately builds on very strong coding agents/harnesses. Code can exist under the hood when it is the best way to execute an agenda, without exposing that complexity as the user's primary interface.\n    - **Git/repository as durable workspace:** where appropriate, explain that an agenda can live in a folder/Git repository containing durable context, agent definitions, instructions/PRDs/tasks and history. Do not require a nontechnical visitor to understand Git before they understand the product.\n- Messaging hierarchy:\n    1. First make the visitor understand the outcome: **a responsibility can keep being handled in the background**.\n    2. Then introduce the word **agenda** and explain it as a durable area of responsibility.\n    3. Show how an agenda contains context + goals/tasks + agents/tools and persists over time.\n    4. Show concrete examples, with self-maintaining software/web as the strongest/most native example.\n    5. Only after the concept is clear explain the technical leverage: strong coding harnesses, repositories, multiple models/vendors.\n- The page must clearly contrast:\n    - **one-shot AI:** \"do this task now\" / impressive but ends after the task,\n    - **agenda:** \"take responsibility for this area over time\" / continues, observes, acts and escalates when needed.\n- Do not frame ChatGPT, Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode or other strong agents as bad or obsolete. The positioning is explicitly that these systems are excellent and Promptbook **builds on their strength** to make them persistent and operational.\n- Avoid generic AI-marketing language such as \"revolutionize your business\", \"AI employee for everything\", or unsupported claims of total autonomy.\n- Avoid over-indexing on the term \"agent\". A visitor should leave remembering **their agenda/responsibility**, not Promptbook's internal agent taxonomy.\n- Avoid automatically adding supporting copy, subheadlines or explanatory filler under every heading. If text does not add new information, omit it. The heading and UI/visual itself should carry the idea whenever possible.\n- Design direction:\n    - Reuse the existing Promptbook visual language where it helps, but redesign sections whose current structure is coupled to the old company-document proposition.\n    - Prefer a visual explanation of the model over walls of prose.\n    - Consider a simple diagram/interactive composition such as `Agenda → context + tasks/goals + agents/tools → continuous background work → outcomes/escalations`, but implement the clearest solution consistent with the current design system.\n    - Make \"one-shot → ongoing agenda\" visually obvious above the fold or immediately after the hero.\n    - The page must remain polished and understandable on mobile, not only desktop.\n- Information architecture:\n    - `/cs` becomes the new Czech agenda-based main homepage.\n    - `/en` should express the same product positioning in natural English, not a literal awkward translation. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_019q7TiEsiq6Zxh1HK5bVetM","type":"tool_result","content":"1\timport { ONLINE_WORKSHOP_PARTICIPANT_PATH } from '@/businesses/online-workshop/config';\n2\t\n3\tconst ADMIN_TRACKING_EXCLUDED_PATH_PREFIXES = ['/admin'] as const;\n4\tconst SENSITIVE_TRACKING_QUERY_PARAMETERS = ['email', 'fullname', 'token'] as const;\n5\t\n6\tfunction isWorkshopParticipantPath(pathname: string): boolean {\n7\t    return pathname === ONLINE_WORKSHOP_PARTICIPANT_PATH || pathname.startsWith(`${ONLINE_WORKSHOP_PARTICIPANT_PATH}/`);\n8\t}\n9\t\n10\tfunction isPathExcluded(pathname: string, excludedPathPrefixes: readonly string[]): boolean {\n11\t    return excludedPathPrefixes.some(\n12\t        (excludedPrefix) => pathname === excludedPrefix || pathname.startsWith(`${excludedPrefix}/`),\n13\t    );\n14\t}\n15\t\n16\t/**\n17\t * Admin URLs carry a bearer token and the participant URL can carry personal\n18\t * data. Neither page may receive normal page tracking or session recording.\n19\t */\n20\texport function isThirdPartyTrackingAllowed(pathname: string): boolean {\n21\t    return !isPathExcluded(pathname, ADMIN_TRACKING_EXCLUDED_PATH_PREFIXES) && !isWorkshopParticipantPath(pathname);\n22\t}\n23\t\n24\t/**\n25\t * The participant room sends only explicit anonymized interaction events to\n26\t * Google Analytics. It never sends its URL as a page view because that URL can\n27\t * temporarily contain a prefilled e-mail address or full name.\n28\t */\n29\texport function isGoogleAnalyticsAllowed(pathname: string): boolean {\n30\t    return !isPathExcluded(pathname, ADMIN_TRACKING_EXCLUDED_PATH_PREFIXES);\n31\t}\n32\t\n33\texport function isGoogleAnalyticsPageViewAllowed(pathname: string): boolean {\n34\t    return isGoogleAnalyticsAllowed(pathname) && !isWorkshopParticipantPath(pathname);\n35\t}\n36\t\n37\t/**\n38\t * Defense in depth for any URL recorded before a page-level exclusion takes\n39\t * effect, including same-origin API calls.\n40\t */\n41\texport function removeSensitiveTrackingParameters(url: string): string {\n42\t    try {\n43\t        const parsedUrl = new URL(\n44\t            url,\n45\t            typeof window === 'undefined' ? The studio now decides in one place what a usable index is, from\n  a bounded read of the container's head and tail rather than from its media, and checks every part the moment it\n  closes, at a global pause as well as at Stop. The verdict stays on that part, and both the individual\n  **Stáhnout originál** and the originals inside a ZIP are handed over inside a proper indexed container, rebuilt by\n  forced packet copy through the same temporary working file trimming already uses: not one packet is re-encoded, no\n  timestamp is shifted, the result is accepted only when it really is seekable and still covers the measured\n  recorded range, and the committed capture bytes in the browser or the chosen folder are never rewritten. Where no\n  index can be built — an unsupported codec, no working storage, a rebuilt file too large to download without a disk\n  picker, or a result which fails that check — the recorder's own bytes are handed over unchanged and the reason is\n  written into `recording.json` beside each part's index status and explained in the archive `README.txt`. An index\n  which cannot be checked at all, or which this browser could never rebuild, is announced through the existing alert\n  channel with the exact `ffmpeg` command, so the administrator hears it while they are still in the room; because\n  nothing was lost and nothing stopped, such a take stays complete and remains available for **Donahrát**. Trimmed\n  files always carried an index and are unchanged. Exactly what I needed. 🙌',\n                    startDelay: 1000,\n                    static: false,\n                },\n            ],\n        },\n        socialProof: {\n            eyebrow: 'For companies that take their data seriously',\n            industries: [\n                'Manufacturing',\n                'Law firms',\n                'Construction',\n                'Public administration',\n                'Healthcare',\n                'Education',\n                'Logistics',\n                'Energy',\n                'IT',\n                'Insurance',\n                'Pharma',\n                'E-commerce',\n                'Accounting firms',\n                'Telecom',\n            ],\n        },\n        painPoints: {\n            eyebrow: 'Why companies lose millions',\n            heading: (\n                <>\n                    The knowledge is already in your company.{' '}\n                    <span className=\"bg-gradient-to-r from-[#0891b2] to-[#06b6d4] bg-clip-text text-transparent\">\n                        Nobody can find it.\n                    </span>\n                </>\n            ),\n            points: [\n                {\n                    title: 'Scattered company data',\n                    description:\n                        \"Policies on SharePoint, contracts in email, manuals on Google Drive, processes in people's heads. It's just spread across dozens of systems.\",\n                    consequence: 'Employees search instead of doing the work you pay them for.',\n                },\n                {\n                    title: 'Key people as an internal help desk',\n                    description:\n                        'Senior people answer the same questions over and over, from newcomers and colleagues alike. Public AI doesn't know your company. That's why we built it differently.\",\n                },\n                {\n                    title: '\"I don\\'t know\" beats a hallucination',\n                    description:\n                        \"Public AI invents five paragraphs that sound convincing. They can cost you the company. Promptbook draws only from your data. A new hire\n                    can ask, and so can a seasoned manager. Both get the same precise answer.\n                </>\n            ),\n            cta: 'I want a free strategy call',\n            badges: ['100% GDPR', 'Up to 1,000,000 standard pages', 'Czech platform'],\n            chatTitle: 'Promptbook - HR Assistant',\n            chatInputPlaceholder: 'Type a question...',\n            chatMessages: [\n                {\n                    id: 1,\n                    type: 'user',\n                    text: \"Hi, I just started here and I can't find how many vacation days I get. According to the employee handbook, you get **25 vacation days per year**.',\n                    startDelay: 2000,\n                    static: false,\n                },\n                {\n                    id: 3,\n                    type: 'bot',\n                    text: \"I'll email it to you as well, so you have it handy. Anything else?\",\n                    startDelay: 1200,\n                    static: false,\n                },\n                {\n                    id: 4,\n                    type: 'user',\n                    text: 'Great, thanks! Exactly what I needed. 🙌',\n                    startDelay: 1000,\n                    static: false,\n                },\n            ],\n        },\n        socialProof: {\n            eyebrow: 'For companies that take their data seriously',\n            industries: [\n                'Manufacturing',\n                'Law firms',\n                'Construction',\n                'Public administration',\n                'Healthcare',\n                'Education',\n                'Logistics',\n                'Energy',\n                'IT',\n                'Insurance',\n                'Pharma',\n                'E-commerce',\n                'Accounting firms',\n                'Telecom',\n            ],\n        },\n        painPoints: {\n            eyebrow: 'Why companies lose millions',\n            heading: (\n                <>\n                    The knowledge is already in your company.{' '}\n                    <span className=\"bg-gradient-to-r from-[#0891b2] to-[#06b6d4] bg-clip-text text-transparent\">\n                        Nobody can find it.\n                    </span>\n                </>\n            ),\n            points: [\n                {\n                    title: 'Scattered company data',\n                    description:\n                        \"Policies on SharePoint, contracts in email, manuals on Google Drive, processes in people's heads. It all exists. It's just spread across dozens of systems.\",\n                    consequence: 'Employees search instead of doing the work you pay them for.',\n                },\n                {\n                    title: 'Key people as an internal help desk',\n                    description:\n                        'Senior people answer the same questions over and over, from newcomers and colleagues alike. Instead of strategic work, they run an information desk.',\n                    consequence: 'Your most expensive people are doing work a system should be doing.',\n                },\n                {\n                    title: 'Public AI risk',\n                    description:\n                        \"People paste work into public ChatGPT, sensitive company documents included. Public AI doesn't know your company. When it doesn't have the answer, it makes one up.\",\n                    consequence:\n                        'One decision based on invented information can cost more than your whole annual software budget.',\n                },\n                {\n                    title: 'Departing know-how',\n                    description:\n                        'When an experienced person leaves, they take knowledge nobody wrote down. How decisions get made, what each client has been through, why things are done this way.',\n                    consequence: \"The company loses years of experience, and you don't get that back quickly.\",\n                },\n            ],\n            timeAllocation: {\n                title: \"Where does your team's time go?\",\n                beforeLabel: 'Before',\n                beforePrimary: 'Busywork',\n                beforeSecondary: '20%',\n                beforeNote: 'Emails · Meetings · Routine tasks',\n                afterLabel: 'After deploying Promptbook',\n                afterPrimary: 'What matters',\n                afterSecondary: '20%',\n                afterNote: 'Family · Creativity · Strategic work',\n            },\n        },\n        solution: {\n            eyebrow: 'Solution',\n            heading: (\n                <>\n                    A virtual employee who{' '}\n                    <span className=\"bg-gradient-to-r from-[#0891b2] to-[#06b6d4] bg-clip-text text-transparent\">\n                        knows the whole company.\n                    </span>\n                </>\n            ),\n            description:\n                'Upload your company documents into a secure vault. Promptbook turns them into a virtual employee: an HR specialist, a lawyer, a technician. Then anyone can just ask, in plain language.',\n            benefits: [\n                {\n                    title: 'No prompting',\n                    description:\n                        'No training. No \"write the prompt like an IT person would\". Your people are experts in their field, not in casting spells on robots. They ask, by text or by voice, and they get an answer.',\n                    highlight: 'The same way they talk to a colleague.',\n                },\n                {\n                    title: 'Context vault',\n                    description:\n                        \"Data never leaves your infrastructure. We don't use it to train any models. Do you know what happens when an employee pastes an NDA into public ChatGPT?\",\n                    highlight: \"We do. That's why we built it differently.\",\n                },\n                {\n                    title: '\"I don\\'t know\" beats a hallucination',\n                    description:\n                        \"Public AI invents five paragraphs that sound convincing. They can cost you the company. Promptbook draws only from your data. And when it can't find the answer?\",\n                    highlight: 'It says it straight: \"I don\\'t have that information in your documents.\"',\n                },\n            ],\n        },\n        howItWorks: {\n            eyebrow: 'How it works',\n            heading: (\n                <>\n                    Deployment{' '}\n                    <span className=\"bg-gradient-to-r from-[#0891b2] to-[#06b6d4] bg-clip-text text-transparent\">\n                        without the pain.\n                    </span>\n                </>\n            ),\n            steps: [\n                {\n                    title: 'Upload documents',\n                    description:\n                        'Policies, contracts, manuals, NDAs, meeting notes. Anything sitting today in SharePoint, on Google Drive, or in a desk drawer. Promptbook handles up to one million standard pages.',\n                },\n                {\n                    title: 'Create a virtual employee',\n                    description:\n                        'An HR specialist who knows the employee handbook. A lawyer who knows every contract. A technician who knows the manuals. Each agent answers strictly from your company data.',\n                },\n                {\n                    title: 'People ask questions',\n                    description:\n                        'In plain language. Like sending a WhatsApp message. Or a voice note. No prompts, no training, no IT department.',\n                },\n            ],\n            cta: 'I want to see how it works',\n        },\n        enemy: {\n            eyebrow: 'Why not public ChatGPT',\n            heading: (\n                <>\n                    &quot;I&apos;ll just paste it into ChatGPT&quot;{' '}\n                    <span className=\"bg-gradient-to-r from-red-500 to-rose-500 bg-clip-text text-transparent\">\n                        is corporate self-sabotage.\n                    </span>\n                </>\n            ),\n            chatgptLabel: 'Public ChatGPT',\n            promptbookLabel: 'Promptbook',\n            comparisons: [\n                {\n                    feature: \"When it doesn't know\",\n                    chatgpt: 'Confidently invents one',\n                    promptbook: 'Says: \"I don\\'t know\"',\n                },\n                {\n                    feature: 'Your company data',\n                    chatgpt: 'Public cloud. Who knows who reads it',\n                    promptbook: 'Locked in your vault',\n                },\n                {\n                    feature: 'Training on your data',\n                    chatgpt: 'Yes, it trains other models on it',\n                    promptbook: 'No. Never.',\n                },\n                {\n                    feature: 'How you ask',\n                    chatgpt: '\"Act as senior lawyer, temperature 0.2...\"',\n                    promptbook: '\"Hey, where\\'s that NDA from 2021?\"',\n                },\n                {\n                    feature: 'Company context',\n                    chatgpt: 'None. It knows nothing about your company',\n                    promptbook: 'It knows your policies, contracts, processes',\n                },\n            ],\n        },\n        testimonials: {\n            eyebrow: 'Testimonials',\n            heading: (\n                <>\n                    What companies say once they{' '}\n                    <span className=\"bg-gradient-to-r from-[#0891b2] to-[#06b6d4] bg-clip-text text-transparent\">\n                        stop searching.\n                    </span>\n                </>\n            ),\n            items: [\n                {\n                    quote: \"Promptbook didn't cut us off from each other. response.headers()['location'];\n    expect(locationHeader, `Expected ${path} to name where it redirects`).toBeDefined();\n\n    return readRedirectDestinationPath(locationHeader, response.url());\n}\n\nfor (const path of PUBLIC_PAGE_PATHS) {\n    // Next.js compiles a route on its first dev-server visit. '';\n\n            const isPromptbookIdentityAbsent = identityTags\n                .filter((element) => /application-name|creator|publisher|og:site_name|twitter:site/.test(element.outerHTML))\n                .every((element) => !element.outerHTML.includes('Promptbook'));\n            const isPromptbookStructuredDataAbsent = structuredDataNodes.every(\n                (element) => !(element.textContent ?? element.getAttribute('rel') === 'apple-touch-icon' &&\n                    element.getAttribute('href') === rasterIconPath,\n            );\n            const isPodcastManifestUsed = isPodcastRssFeedAdvertised = identityTags.some(\n                (element) =>\n                    element.getAttribute('rel') === 'alternate' &&\n                    element.getAttribute('type') ===            (element) => element.textContent?.trim() === rssFeedLabel && element.getAttribute('href') === rssFeedUrl,\n            );\n            const isLegalCompanyPresent = footerText.includes('AI Web s.r.o.');\n\n            return {\n                isPromptbookIdentityAbsent,\n                isPromptbookStructuredDataAbsent,\n                isPodcastIconUsed,\n                isPodcastTouchIconUsed,\n                isPodcastManifestUsed,\n                isPodcastRssFeedAdvertised,\n                isPodcastRssFeedLinked,\n                isLegalCompanyPresent,\n            };\n        },\n        {\n            scalableIconPath: AI_TA_KRAJTA_APP_ICONS.SCALABLE.path,\n            rasterIconPath: AI_TA_KRAJTA_APP_ICONS.RASTER.path,\n            manifestPath: AI_TA_KRAJTA_MANIFEST_PATH,\n            rssFeedMediaType: AI_TA_KRAJTA_RSS_FEED_MEDIA_TYPE,\n            rssFeedUrl: AI_TA_KRAJTA_RSS_FEED_PLATFORM.url,\n            rssFeedLabel: AI_TA_KRAJTA_RSS_FEED_PLATFORM.label,\n        },\n    );\n\n    expect(metadataIdentity).toEqual({\n        isPromptbookIdentityAbsent: true,\n        isPromptbookStructuredDataAbsent: true,\n        isPodcastIconUsed: true,\n        isPodcastTouchIconUsed: true,\n        isPodcastManifestUsed: true,\n        isPodcastRssFeedAdvertised: true,\n        isPodcastRssFeedLinked: true,\n        isLegalCompanyPresent: true,\n    });\n\n    await expect(page.locator('footer').getByRole('link', { name: 'Done by Promptbook coder', exact: true }))\n        .toHaveAttribute('href', 'https://coder.ptbk.io/');\n\n    const manifestResponse = await page.request.get(AI_TA_KRAJTA_MANIFEST_PATH);\n\n    expect(manifestResponse.ok()).toBeTruthy();\n    expect(await manifestResponse.json()).toMatchObject({\n        name: AI_TA_KRAJTA_BRAND_NAME,\n        short_name: AI_TA_KRAJTA_BRAND_NAME,\n        icons: [\n            { src: AI_TA_KRAJTA_APP_ICONS.SCALABLE.path, purpose: 'any' },\n            { src: AI_TA_KRAJTA_APP_ICONS.RASTER.path, purpose: 'any' },\n            { src: AI_TA_KRAJTA_APP_ICONS.RASTER.path, purpose: expect(iconResponse.headers()['content-type']).toContain(appIcon.type);\n    }\n});\n\ntest('AI ta Krajta searches complete transcripts on the server without sending them to the browser', async ({   };\n        },\n        {\n            scalableIconPath: AI_TA_KRAJTA_APP_ICONS.SCALABLE.path,\n            rasterIconPath: AI_TA_KRAJTA_APP_ICONS.RASTER.path,\n            manifestPath: isPodcastIconUsed: true,\n        isPodcastTouchIconUsed: true,\n        isPodcastManifestUsed: true,\n        isPodcastRssFeedAdvertised: true,\n        isPodcastRssFeedLinked: true,\n   PRO_FIRMY_PATH,\n    '/pro-mesta',\n    '/for-agro',\n    '/for-industry',\n    '/ai-supervize',\n    AI_SUPERVIZE_MINI_PATH,\n    // '/ai-supervize-mini',\n    '/ai-ta-krajta',\n    AI_TA_KRAJTA_MEDIA_KIT_PATH,\n    AI_TA_KRAJTA_BRANDING_PATH,\n    '/hackathon-factory',\n    '/cs/online-workshop',\n    '/cs/komunita/clenstvi',\n    '/cs/pavol',\n    '/en/pavol',\n
