const;\n\ntype PublicPagePath = (typeof PUBLIC_PAGE_PATHS)[number];\n\n/**\n * The address which used to hold the training and now only forwards to the workshop it became\n */\nconst RETIRED_TRAINING_PATH = '/skoleni';\n\n/**\n * A public address which renders nothing itself and only forwards to a page of this suite.\n *\n * Note: A route reading `Accept-Language` may pick any of its localized destinations, so every one of them is\n *       accepted and every one of them is rendered by its own page check above.\n */\ntype PublicRedirect = {\n    readonly path: string;\n    readonly statusCode: number;\n    readonly destinationPaths: readonly PublicPagePath[];\n};\n\nconst PERMANENT_REDIRECT_STATUS_CODE = 308;\nconst TEMPORARY_REDIRECT_STATUS_CODE = 307;\n\nconst PUBLIC_REDIRECTS: readonly PublicRedirect[] = [\n    { path: '/', statusCode: TEMPORARY_REDIRECT_STATUS_CODE, destinationPaths: ['/cs', '/en'] },\n    { path: '/pavol', statusCode: TEMPORARY_REDIRECT_STATUS_CODE, destinationPaths: ['/cs/pavol', '/en/pavol'] },\n    {\n        path: '/privacy',\n        statusCode: TEMPORARY_REDIRECT_STATUS_CODE,\n        destinationPaths: ['/cs/ochrana-osobnich-udaju', '/en/privacy-policy'],\n    },\n    {\n        path: '/terms',\n        statusCode: TEMPORARY_REDIRECT_STATUS_CODE,\n        destinationPaths: ['/cs/obchodni-podminky', '/en/terms-and-conditions'],\n    },\n    {\n        path: RETIRED_TRAINING_PATH,\n        statusCode: PERMANENT_REDIRECT_STATUS_CODE,\n        destinationPaths: [AI_SUPERVIZE_MINI_PATH],\n    },\n];\n\nconst E2E_DISCOUNT_CODE = 'E2E SLEVA';\n\nconst PUBLIC_PAGE_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 180_000;\n\nasync function expectPublicPageToLoad(page: Page, path: PublicPagePath): Promise<void> {\n    const response = await page.goto(path, { waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded' });\n\n    expect(response, `Expected ${path} to produce a document response`).not.toBeNull();\n    expect(response!.ok(), `Expected ${path} to load without a server error`).toBeTruthy();\n    await expect(\n        page.locator('main, h1, footer').first(),\n        `Expected ${path} to render visible page content`,\n    ).toBeVisible();\n}\n\n/**\n * Reads where a redirect points, whether it answers with an absolute or a site-relative `Location`.\n */\nfunction readRedirectDestinationPath(locationHeader: string, requestUrl: string): string {\n    const destinationUrl = new URL(locationHeader, requestUrl);\n\n    return `${destinationUrl.pathname}${destinationUrl.search}${destinationUrl.hash}`;\n}\n\n/**\n * Asks a redirecting address where it points without following it, so the destination is rendered once by the page\n * check which owns it instead of a second time through every address leading to it.\n */\nasync function readRedirectDestination(\n    request: APIRequestContext,\n    path: string,\n    expectedStatusCode: number,\n): Promise<string> {\n    const response = await request.get(path, { maxRedirects: 0 });\n\n    expect(response.status(), `Expected ${path} to answer with status ${expectedStatusCode}`).toBe(expectedStatusCode);\n\n    const locationHeader = response.headers()['location'];\n    expect(locationHeader, `Expected ${path} to name where it redirects`).toBeDefined();\n\n    return readRedirectDestinationPath(locationHeader, response.url());\n}\n\nfor (const path of PUBLIC_PAGE_PATHS) {\n    // Next.js compiles a route on its first dev-server visit. Isolating every route keeps earlier cold compilations\n    // from exhausting the timeout of a healthy page later in the smoke suite.\n    test(`public landing and information page loads: ${path}`, async ({ page }) => {\n        await expectPublicPageToLoad(page, path);\n    });\n}\n\ntest('AI ta Krajta collaboration section deep-links to its media kit', async ({ page }) => {\n    await page.goto(AI_TA_KRAJTA_PATH, { waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded' });\n\n    const mediaKitLink = page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Otevřít media kit' });\n    await expect(mediaKitLink).toHaveAttribute('href', AI_TA_KRAJTA_MEDIA_KIT_PATH);\n    await mediaKitLink.click();\n\n    await expect(page).toHaveURL(AI_TA_KRAJTA_MEDIA_KIT_PATH);\n    await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /Oslovte české a slovenské publikum/i })).toBeVisible();\n});\n\ntest('AI ta Krajta owns its metadata, icon and installable manifest and credits Promptbook coder', async ({ page }) => {\n    await page.goto(AI_TA_KRAJTA_PATH, { waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded' });\n    await expect(page.locator('footer')).toBeVisible();\n    await expect(page).toHaveTitle(`${AI_TA_KRAJTA_BRAND_NAME} | Český podcast o umělé inteligenci`);\n\n    const metadataIdentity = await page.evaluate(\n        ({ scalableIconPath, rasterIconPath, manifestPath, rssFeedMediaType, rssFeedUrl, rssFeedLabel }) => {\n            const identityTags = Array.from(document.head.querySelectorAll('meta, link'));\n            const structuredDataNodes = Array.from(document.head.querySelectorAll('script[type*=ld]'));\n            const footerText = document.querySelector('footer')?.textContent ?? '';\n\n            const isPromptbookIdentityAbsent = identityTags\n                .filter((element) => /application-name|creator|publisher|og:site_name|twitter:site/.test(element.outerHTML))\n                .every((element) => !element.outerHTML.includes('Promptbook'));\n            const isPromptbookStructuredDataAbsent = structuredDataNodes.every(\n                (element) => !(element.textContent ?? '').includes('Promptbook'),\n            );\n            const isPodcastIconUsed = identityTags.some(\n                (element) =>\n                    element.getAttribute('rel') === 'icon' && element.getAttribute('href') === scalableIconPath,\n            );\n            const isPodcastTouchIconUsed = identityTags.some(\n                (element) =>\n                    element.getAttribute('rel') === 'apple-touch-icon' &&\n                    element.getAttribute('href') === rasterIconPath,\n            );\n            const isPodcastManifestUsed = identityTags.some(\n                (element) => element.getAttribute('rel') === 'manifest' && element.getAttribute('href') === manifestPath,\n            );\n            const isPodcastRssFeedAdvertised = identityTags.some(\n                (element) =>\n                    element.getAttribute('rel') === 'alternate' &&\n                    element.getAttribute('type') === rssFeedMediaType &&\n                    element.getAttribute('href') === rssFeedUrl,\n            );\n            const isPodcastRssFeedLinked = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('a')).some(\n                (element) => element.textContent?.trim() === rssFeedLabel && element.getAttribute('href') === rssFeedUrl,\n            );\n            const isLegalCompanyPresent = footerText.includes('AI isPodcastTouchIconUsed,\n                isPodcastManifestUsed,\n                isPodcastRssFeedAdvertised,\n                isPodcastRssFeedLinked,\n                isLegalCompanyPresent,\n            };\n        },\n        {\n            scalableIconPath: AI_TA_KRAJTA_APP_ICONS.SCALABLE.path,\n            rasterIconPath: AI_TA_KRAJTA_APP_ICONS.RASTER.path,\n            manifestPath: AI_TA_KRAJTA_MANIFEST_PATH,\n            rssFeedMediaType: AI_TA_KRAJTA_RSS_FEED_MEDIA_TYPE,\n            rssFeedUrl: AI_TA_KRAJTA_RSS_FEED_PLATFORM.url,\n            rssFeedLabel: AI_TA_KRAJTA_RSS_FEED_PLATFORM.label,\n        },\n    );\n\n    expect(metadataIdentity).toEqual({\n        isPromptbookIdentityAbsent: true,\n        isPromptbookStructuredDataAbsent: true,\n        isPodcastIconUsed: true,\n        isPodcastTouchIconUsed: true,\n        isPodcastManifestUsed: true,\n        isPodcastRssFeedAdvertised: true,\n        isPodcastRssFeedLinked: true,\n        isLegalCompanyPresent: true,\n    });\n\n    await expect(page.locator('footer').getByRole('link', { name: 'Done by Promptbook coder', exact: true }))\n        .toHaveAttribute('href', manifestResponse.json()).toMatchObject({\n        name: AI_TA_KRAJTA_BRAND_NAME,\n        short_name: AI_TA_KRAJTA_BRAND_NAME,\n        icons: [\n            { src: AI_TA_KRAJTA_APP_ICONS.SCALABLE.path, purpose: 'any' },\n            { src: AI_TA_KRAJTA_APP_ICONS.RASTER.path, purpose: 'any' },\n            { src: AI_TA_KRAJTA_APP_ICONS.RASTER.path, purpose: 'maskable' },\n        ],\n    });\n\n    for (const appIcon of [AI_TA_KRAJTA_APP_ICONS.SCALABLE, AI_TA_KRAJTA_APP_ICONS.RASTER]) {\n        const iconResponse = await page.request.get(appIcon.path);\n\n        expect(iconResponse.ok(), `Expected ${appIcon.path} to be served`).toBeTruthy();\n        expect(iconResponse.headers()['content-type']).toContain(appIcon.type);\n    }\n});\n\ntest('AI ta Krajta searches complete transcripts on the server without sending them to the browser', async ({ Who may read one answer is decided\n  once, in `lib/workshops/workshopPollOptionVisibility.ts`.\n  Workshops may display and accept votes, but the community owns administration.\n  Where a room puts its polls is decided once, in\n  `lib/workshops/workshopPollPlacement.ts`: the community, which decides in its\n  own polls, opens with them, while a workshop, which is only their subject,\n  keeps them below the materials it was held for.\n- The participant room owns the membership badge and popup. Community and live\n  workshop rooms use the same membership for the connecting email, and checkout\n  returns to the room where it started. Membership is offered only by room kinds\n  listed in `lib/workshops/workshopKindCapabilities.ts`; project discussions do\n  not offer it.\n- Members can open Stripe Customer Portal from the popup. In-app cancellation\n  stops only the next renewal, preserves access through the paid period, appears\n  in the badge, and can be reversed before that period ends.\n- A full-price-for-the-whole-term discount is a voucher: atomically consume it,\n  create membership immediately, ask for no card, and create no Stripe renewal.\n  A limited-month discount still opens checkout because the regular price returns.\n  Stripe webhooks update completed, cancelled, failed, and late payments. With no\n  Stripe key, hide membership; with test keys, identify the test payment gate.\n- Community projects use a URL-first metadata wizard. Ordinary submissions await\n  AI or manual moderation; trusted members and moderators are approved immediately. Pending\n  projects remain visible to their author and moderators.\n- A live workshop room has a countdown before it starts and, while it runs, the\n  event's selected primary stage content: video, presentation, or the connected\n  repository. Existing and unset choices mean video. Other configured sources\n  stay in the shared special-material list, with recordings still selected by\n  the server's member access rule. After the recorded end, the stage returns to\n  the wrap-up. Permanent rooms such as the community do not gain a stage. The\n  room also has reactions, watching count, moderated chat, timed materials, and\n  attached poll aggregates. An open-ended term runs until its recorded end; its\n  stage does not end automatically. Admins\n  can select, replace, clear, or create the displayed comment through the same\n  private realtime channel used by reactions.\n- Workshop and community chat can use reusable Book agents, administered in their shared Agents tab with\n  `BookEditor` from `@promptbook/components`. `LiteAgent` from `@promptbook/node` uses `OPENAI_API_KEY`; definitions\n  are shared while replies, listening and cooldowns are enabled per room. Only newly approved comments enqueue\n  replies, including artificial and other agent messages, with at most two agent turns. A durable database queue\n  owns leases, deduplication and rechecks of moderation, agent settings and room state before publication.\n  Public messages use the existing chat rendering; admin projections and exports distinguish `user`, `artificial`\n  and `agent` origins with agent/run provenance. Agents have no participant sessions or membership access.\n  Live questions require an administrator's active stream-tab or microphone capture in the Agents tab; audio is\n  transcribed in short standalone segments and never saved. Private transcripts feed the agents only during an\n  ongoing workshop and only from its current, unexpired capture session. Stopping capture or ending the workshop\n  prevents its pending live questions from publishing; publication locks that session against a concurrent stop.\n  Project rooms and externally organized events offer no agents. Persistent servers run the queue in the background;\n  serverless hosts can use the authenticated scheduler route documented in `README.md`.\n- A term can be about a project. The connection is one value — GitHub repository,\n  the default branch, and one or more branch patterns such as `main`, `client-*`,\n  `feature/*`, or `*` for all branches, plus any number of public deployment\n  addresses, written one per line — so it is set, changed, and unset at once and\n  neither branch selection nor deployment\n  outlives its repository. Room kinds which offer it are named in\n  `lib/workshops/workshopKindCapabilities.ts`. The room shows the repository as a\n  special material beside its ordinary materials for every participant, with its\n  links, every deployment and newest commits, marking those which arrive while a\n  participant watches;\n  a newly found commit is broadcast to active rooms and appears on the stage for\n  ten seconds. A selection resolving to multiple branches is shown as a commit\n  graph. Commits come from the public commit feed or keyless API, pooled once per\n  server and cached through the revalidation window; an unreadable feed still\n  leaves the room naming its project. A project deployed once is opened as the live\n  application of the workshop; several deployments are each named by their own\n  address, and the first of them is the one a term card and the participant project panel are previewed from.\n  Both reuse the deployment's image, title and description through the shared project preview; missing metadata or\n  a broken image keeps the deployment address visible, with repository-only previews reserved for undeployed projects.\n  The participant preview opens that deployment and loads independently of room state and commits, through an\n  authenticated endpoint using the stored project. Changing rooms, repositories or the primary deployment discards\n  stale previews. Community term cards keep their workshop destination.\n  With a repository and no deployment URL, administration offers direct Vercel deployment using private `VERCEL_TOKEN`\n  and optional `VERCEL_TEAM_ID`. One Vercel project per repository stays connected to its original GitHub source and\n  deploys its production branch (initially the default branch), independently of the workshop's history selection.\n  Administration polls the build and fills in its assigned production alias only when ready; the ordinary settings\n  save publishes that URL. Manual URLs, a changed repository, and switching rooms discard stale pending results.\n  Deployment failures show the reported reason and code, targeted recovery steps, and an optional bounded build-log\n  excerpt with credentials redacted. Canceled, blocked, and alias-assignment failures have distinct guidance; missing\n  diagnostics keep fallback checks and the Vercel link available. Only authenticated administration receives them.\n  This adds no workshop data fields; setup and retry behavior are documented in `README.md`.\n  The connection can also carry independent starting and ending commit IDs. Administration previews each commit's\n  message, author and Prague date, and can fill each bound separately from the workshop time (first commit at or after\n  the start, last at or before the end). Bounds are inclusive by commit time across the selected branches. The room\n  initially shows and highlights that range; expanding and paging its graph reveals history outside it while retaining\n  the highlight. An omitted bound leaves that side open; two omitted bounds leave the history unfiltered. Every lookup,\n  autofill and history page uses the same branch selection, and commits belonging only to other branches stay hidden.\n- A workshop can carry one public presentation URL for a PDF, PowerPoint file, or\n  GitHub Markdown page. The room renders it beside ordinary materials through the\n  shared material card, primary action, preview card and flip-to-show QR code, for every participant without making\n  it timed or membership-gated content.\n- Paid-only materials are decided on the server in one pass. Members receive\n  unlocked material; others receive only the published titles as an offer. An\n  untitled item is not named, items are not named before their unlock time, and a\n  room without membership hides paid-only items without naming them.\n- After a workshop ends, its recording is server-gated to members. Others receive\n  the published teaser, or a generic offer when no teaser exists; a term without\n  a recording offers nothing. An administrator writes the recording's start\n  offset as hours, minutes and seconds, while it stays stored, exported and read\n  in seconds; it applies only to that paid replay and never to the countdown or\n  live stream.\n  A workshop can instead select a hosted synchronized recording while preserving its inactive YouTube settings.\n  Direct admin import and studio publication use the same private multipart object storage and schema 5 validation;\n  verified revisions publish atomically, and old revisions remain briefly for connected viewers. Room JSON and every\n  hosted manifest/range request apply the same live/free and paid replay rule. Prepared hosted media uses export zero,\n  with recorded pause gaps mapped to the chosen live wall clock; the YouTube offset is never applied again. Imported\n  subtitle sidecars stay out of the participant player. Cleanup claims inactive revisions before removing objects.\n  The hosted participant player uses one prepared-export clock across Auto, Editor, Aplikace and Kamera, with a camera\n  overlay in Auto, reviewed activity speed boundaries, event markers and anchored commit selection in the existing\n  repository graph. Auto speed advances automatic-coding intervals through decoded steps at up to 10× and waits when\n  decoding is slower. Free live playback serves only the completed, at-most-two-second segment at the server-delayed playhead through a\n  time-authorized route; direct full-file bytes and other segments are denied. Members may seek the full published\n  recording. Complete publication is required before this scheduled live delivery; it is not an ingest stream.\n- Pending chat messages, member-written poll answers, and community projects use\n  `lib/workshops/workshopAutoApproval.ts` for optional AI approval after saving.\n  `WORKSHOP_AUTO_APPROVAL_API_KEY` enables it; the model and HTTPS base URL are\n  configurable. Only clearly suitable content is approved; uncertainty, missing\n  configuration, invalid output, and an eight-second timeout leave it pending.\n  The database approves only unchanged pending content from a currently unbanned\n  author and privately records the item, model, and time. AI never rejects, edits,\n  grants trust, or replaces a human decision. It reviews text and URL metadata,\n  without fetching linked pages or preview images. Moderator-created materials\n  require no review, and old pending submissions are not bulk-processed.\n- Trusted participants remain invisible and their messages are auto-approved.\n  The participant lists in workshop and community administration show three exclusive, complete room counts:\n  moderators, trusted non-moderators, and untrusted non-moderators. Their explicit bulk-trust action confirms a\n  server-reviewed eligible set and updates that room atomically; a changed set requires a fresh confirmation.\n  The separate automatic-trust setting defaults off for every new or duplicated room and is applied only when a new\n  participant identity is inserted. Reconnects and later setting changes never rewrite an existing trust decision.\n  Granting trust or moderator status also approves every pending submission by that room-local participant — chat,\n  member-written poll answers, and community projects — in the same database transaction. Rejected items stay\n  rejected; a ban blocks this approval until it is lifted. The private pending-submission view supplies both this\n  approval and the complete per-person counts in room moderation and administrative participant lists. Community\n  project cards refresh with the room without resetting the submission form.\n  Moderators see pending messages, can approve/reject/correct/pin them, and can\n  trust or silence authors. An administrator in `/admin/workshops` and a moderator\n  in a workshop room can also turn any comment into an ordinary, immediately\n  available material. That preserves the comment in chat, carries its complete\n  Markdown body into the material, and names its author in the material title;\n  both entry points use the shared material creation path, including its short\n  links and room refresh. Workshop and community moderators are appointed in\n  `/admin/workshops`; project authors moderate their own discussions.\n- The room records whether each open browser is actively or passively attended\n  from pointer, typing, scroll, and touch activity. Admin analytics distinguish\n  active computer users from merely open tabs with dashed audience lines.\n- The community's compact gallery shows its five highest-upvoted approved projects\n  and links to the full gallery. Community landing content is read from the live\n  room: expose only anonymous totals, approved messages, and shared projects;\n  show member first names only. If the room cannot be read, show less content,\n  not an error. Landing-page reactions are estimates based on recent room data.\n\n### Administration and data rules\n\n- Workshop and community settings render their shared `WorkshopSettingsForm` directly in the Settings tab,\n  with autosave and navigation protection. Other admin creation and editing use the shared `AdminEditorDialog`\n  (and `AdminEditorButton` for a local trigger).\n  Lists show summaries and edit actions; contact notes and contacted status are edited in the contact dialog.\n  The dialog contains request errors, traps and restores focus, and scrolls within the viewport. Closing with its\n  button or Escape flushes pending saves and keeps invalid or failed drafts open; backdrop clicks preserve the editor.\n  Search, filters, and immediate moderation actions stay in their lists. New records still require explicit creation.\n\n- Existing records in `/admin` autosave through `useAdminAutosave` and the shared `AdminSaveQueue`.\n  Raw drafts remain dirty through validation failures and failed requests; writes are debounced and serialized,\n  and polling must not replace an editor's draft. Editors stay open after autosave. Pending writes protect\n  close/reload with the browser's native warning; admin links, section/record switches, and sign-out flush saves\n  before leaving. Explicit API mutations share `requestAdminJson`/`protectAdminMutation` for in-flight protection.\n  Creation and destructive actions remain explicit. Keep record editors keyed by their stable database identity.\n  Immediate material unlocking shares its draft save. Poll updates return generated prepared-choice IDs; the editor\n  carries them into subsequent saves while preserving newer text, so autosaving never recreates a saved choice.\n\n- Event kinds are defined once in `lib/events/eventTypes.ts`; adding one should\n  not require database migration or page-specific duplication. Terms ask for kind,\n  online/place format, price, and capacity. Each kind also names where its landing\n  page records registrations, which is the `placeName` of the contacts it gathers.\n  A kind which names no landing page is held by somebody else: its terms carry the\n  address they are held at, are refused without one, and this application runs no\n  room, gathers no registration, and returns no payer to them.\n- Which term a registration belongs to is decided once, in\n  `lib/workshops/workshopRegistrations.ts`. A term is recognised by its slug, by\n  its Prague day, and by the moment it begins at, so registrations written before\n  terms had slugs keep counting. Registration forms write the term through the\n  same line prefixes that rule reads back. Contacts are still gathered, recorded\n  and shown only by `/admin/contacts`; counting reads nothing but their notes.\n  The registration actions in workshop administration carry that same term filter\n  into the contacts list and its exports.\n- Workshop polls are read-only in workshop administration, except for the\n  answers members wrote into them: an administrator approves, rejects, rewords,\n  or deletes one together with the votes cast for it, and reads it named by the\n  author who wrote it, while a moderator of the room owning the poll only\n  decides about it from the room itself. Creating a new event\n  publishes it by default; duplicating an event keeps it published unless the\n  source is unpublished. Duplicating a workshop preserves its connections to\n  the already existing attached polls; it creates no polls, options, votes, or room history. Stage settings contain\n  the live stream, paid-recording start offset, and recording teaser; presentation settings the public presentation\n  address, and project settings the repository the term is about, written as an\n  address or as `owner/name`, together with its branch patterns. Deleting a workshop is a soft deletion: its room\n  data and attached\n  community polls stay stored, but the term leaves normal public and administrative\n  lists and no longer holds its slug for a replacement. An end may be empty;\n  admins can record, adjust, clear, and reopen it. Overview analytics are zoomable and share their\n  room, section, lines, reaction, zoom, and keyword metrics through query params.\n- Community administration is the workshop dashboard restricted to the\n  `community` room kind: no room picker, schedule, stage, reactions, or address.\n  Its membership view filters Stripe lifecycle, prices, discounts, identifiers,\n  dates, test/live mode, and links to the exact Stripe checkout/subscription.\n  Community analytics cover all measured time and member details show seen times.\n- Shortener search, provenance filters, sorting, and selected click history live\n  in GET parameters. Editing changes only shortcode, destinations, note, and\n  landing page; deletion also deletes recorded clicks.\n\n### Database and verification\n\n- Put database changes in `migrations/*.sql`. Startup and\n  `npm run migrate-database` run `_initialize.sql`, then migrations in filename\n  order, recording immutable filenames and checksums in `public.\"Migration\"`.\n  Changed or missing migrations fail, as do queries requiring an unapplied one.\n- `npm run test-types` must build before `tsc` to refresh `.next/types`.\n- `npm run test-e2e` uses the Next.js development server; first-request compile\n  headroom belongs in `playwright.config.ts`, not individual tests. E2E tests are\n  independent and retry once in a fresh browser context for transient failures;\n  failed-attempt traces remain available. Each attempt archives one recording in\n  `tests/e2e/videos/`, retaining only recent runs.\n- Recording-studio E2E sources use canvas video and synthesized audio with a silent Web Audio output, independent\n  of physical audio-device clocks. Keep recording, storage, codecs, trimming, and ZIP exports real in these tests.\n  Recorded A/V markers are checked from decoded sample timestamps rather than speaker-output latency. The preparation\n  fixture additionally carries readable/binary timecodes and claps at 25/30 fps with distinct startup offsets.\n  Simulated ten-hour mappings and decoder delays do not establish a ten-hour capture soak or physical macOS behavior.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":26,"oldLines":7,"newStart":26,"newLines":18,"lines":[" - `/` redirects to `/cs` or `/en` using `Accept-Language`."," - `/cs` is the Czech homepage and source of truth for homepage structure and copy."," - `/en` is its English localization.","-- `/pro-mesta`, `/pro-firmy`, `/for-agro`, `/for-industry`, `/ai-supervize`,","+- `/cs/pro-firmy` is the Czech company-data landing page: company documents, a virtual","+  employee answering in plain language, GDPR, and a strategic call. It owns that","+  proposition — its composition in `businesses/pro-firmy/_ProFirmyPage.tsx`, every word","+  in `businesses/pro-firmy/proFirmyContent.tsx`, and its own metadata, canonical URL,","+  sharing card and sitemap entry in `businesses/pro-firmy/proFirmyMetadata.ts`. It is","+  published in Czech only and names no language alternate. `/cs` and `/en` render that","+  same composition until the homepage is repositioned; repositioning means composing the","+  homepage from sections and content of its own, never changing the preserved ones.","+  The legacy `/pro-firmy` permanently redirects there. The header's own default copy is","+  site chrome and lives beside it in `components/headerContent.ts`, so no landing page","+  owns the words every other page wears.","+- `/pro-mesta`, `/for-agro`, `/for-industry`, `/ai-supervize`,","   `/hackathon-factory`, and `/pavol` are specialized landing pages. `/pavol`","   redirects to `/cs/pavol` or `/en/pavol`; those legacy Promptbook paths then","   permanently redirect to Pavol Hejny's Czech `https://pavolhejny.cz/` and English"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false}}

Nothing was redesigned, so the header and its strategic-call button,\n  the animated assistant conversation, the industries, pain points, solution, how-it-works, the comparison, the\n  testimonials and metrics, the team, the final call to action, the qualification popup, the booking notice and the\n  footer all read and behave as they did, on a phone as well as on a desktop, and the qualification form still\n  records its lead through the same contact source and thank-you page. Nothing was redesigned, so the header and its strategic-call button,\n  the animated assistant conversation, the industries, pain points, solution, how-it-works, the comparison, the\n  testimonials and metrics, the team, the final call to action, the qualification popup, the booking notice and the\n  footer all read and behave as they did, on a phone as well as on a desktop, and the qualification form still\n  records its lead through the same contact source and thank-you page. The default header copy every public page wears moved out of the\n  landing page's content into `components/headerContent.ts`, where the header which falls back to it lives.","originalFile":"# Current preversion\n\n- Recording-studio files no longer leave the studio without a seek index. A browser recorder writes a live container\n  — the Matroska `Segment` keeps an unknown size, no `Cues` are written and no duration is stored — so every original\n  played from the beginning but could not be seeked in, which is what the manual\n  `ffmpeg -i … -map 0 -c copy …` repair was fixing. The studio now decides in one place what a usable index is, from\n  a bounded read of the container's head and tail rather than from its media, and checks every part the moment it\n  closes, at a global pause as well as at Stop. The verdict stays on that part, and both the individual\n  **Stáhnout originál** and the originals inside a ZIP are handed over inside a proper indexed container, rebuilt by\n  forced packet copy through the same temporary working file trimming already uses: not one packet is re-encoded, no\n  timestamp is shifted, the result is accepted only when it really is seekable and still covers the measured\n  recorded range, and the committed capture bytes in the browser or the chosen folder are never rewritten. Where no\n  index can be built — an unsupported codec, no working storage, a rebuilt file too large to download without a disk\n  picker, or a result which fails that check — the recorder's own bytes are handed over unchanged and the reason is\n  written into `recording.json` beside each part's index status and explained in the archive `README.txt`. An index\n  which cannot be checked at all, or which this browser could never rebuild, is announced through the existing alert\n  channel with the exact `ffmpeg` command, so the administrator hears it while they are still in the room; because\n  nothing was lost and nothing stopped, such a take stays complete and remains available for **Donahrát**. Trimmed\n  files always carried an index and are unchanged. Analysis, the contract and its limits are in\n  `docs/recording-studio-seek-index.md`.\n\n- A recording-studio failure now keeps recording whatever it can and always says so out loud. Losing a camera, a\n  shared window or a microphone stops only that source's track, leaves the rest of the session in it as a gap and\n  lets the other sources record on the same clock; the take itself ends only when nothing is left to record or when\n  the shared storage fails. Every failure — including a stopped, crashed or out-of-space recording — goes through one\n  channel which shows it on the source card and the page, plays an alert sound and posts a browser notification, so\n  an administrator working in the very application being recorded is told without watching the studio tab. Sound and\n  notifications can be turned off separately, are remembered in this browser only, and an explicit **Otestovat\n  výstrahu** button raises a real alert through the real channels before a recording needs them. A take which lost a\n  source is saved as interrupted and names every source it lost.\n\n- Added a shared-clock participant player for hosted workshop recordings with Auto/Editor/Aplikace/Kamera views,\n  camera picture-in-picture, one audible track, event and activity timeline, manual speed and reviewed automatic\n  coding intervals at up to 10×. The existing repository graph highlights the verified anchored SHA at the playhead.\n  Free live viewers receive only the independently remuxed, at-most-two-second segment at the server-delayed playhead; full media byte ranges,\n  past and future segments remain server-gated, while members can seek the complete published recording. The existing\n  YouTube stage, supplementary placement, wrap-up and paid replay offer remain in use. Slow decoders make accelerated\n  navigation wait for a decoded frame rather than desynchronize the tracks. Delivery and publication limits are in\n  `docs/workshop-hosted-player.md`.\n\n- Added private, synchronized hosted recordings for workshop video: direct independent file/sidecar import and a\n  studio **Publish to workshop** action share resumable SHA-256 checked multipart S3 uploads. Schema 5 manifests,\n  prepared timing, codecs, optional metadata and subtitles are verified before an atomic revision switch. Admins get\n  an error report and preview; incomplete files never replace the published revision. Participant requests for the\n  manifest and every media byte range recheck room access and the existing live/free versus paid replay rule. A\n  connected viewer keeps one immutable revision during replacement; abandoned uploads and old revisions have guarded\n  cleanup. Verified unpublished revisions can be resumed for publication after a reload; draft files can be replaced.\n  Existing YouTube settings, teaser, offset and stage choice remain available when switching sources.\n\n- Added browser-local workshop player metadata to the synchronized recording editor: reviewed activity intervals,\n  independent event markers, validated Auto-view scene choices, repository/start SHA and reviewed commit anchors.\n  Speech suggests boundaries only; unclassified gaps stay at 1× and never become automatic coding from silence.\n  Git timestamp proposals require an explicit wall-clock/session calibration and verification against selected branches;\n  confirmed missing SHA references report unavailable, while failed GitHub checks remain unknown. Manual edits survive\n  derived-track regeneration, appended takes and selected-directory reloads; scene validation checks actual video.\n  Manifest schema 5 and original/prepared JSON sidecars use the shared IN/OUT recipe, retain original coordinates and\n  report stale source revisions. This is local metadata for a later player, not published media or visible transcript\n  subtitles. Design and limits are documented in `docs/recording-studio-workshop-metadata.md`.\n\n- Added independent browser-local subtitle and speech-activity revisions to the synchronized recording editor.\n  A finished camera/screen audio stream or standalone microphone is selected for each explicit request; older\n  recordings locally verify actual audio before enabling a source. Czech,\n  English and mixed subtitles reuse the authenticated OpenAI transcription route, while local Silero VAD produces\n  speech, silence, uncertain and unavailable intervals without invented confidence. Overlapping subtitle chunks\n  reconcile matching suggestions while keeping cues recognized by only one chunk. Shared session timing survives\n  offsets, pauses and appended takes. Editable lanes, autosave, undo, progress/cancel/retry and stale-revision labels\n  preserve corrected captions and original media. ZIP and individual source exports include UTF-8 SRT/WebVTT and\n  activity JSON/CSV beside source files, with prepared metadata clipped and rebased to the same IN/OUT as prepared\n  media. Manifest schema 4 distinguishes original and prepared coordinates. Implementation analysis, formats and\n  platform verification limits are in `docs/recording-studio-derived-tracks.md`.\n\n- Extended the shared recording workspace with a persistent live monitor (grid, focused source, pinned source,\n  optional tile hiding/minimizing, preview sound and camera mirroring). Those display settings never change armed\n  capture sources or raw files. A single guarded Pause/Resume closes every source into independently playable,\n  durably checkpointed parts and resumes them on a recorded-content clock without paused wall time. Failed\n  restart, device loss or storage failure interrupts the entire take and retains committed parts. Editing now has\n  **Donahrát do tohoto projektu**: it restores the intended sources, waits for renewed permissions and explicit\n  Start, then appends a new take under the same recording ID. Old media and edits remain; an untouched full range\n  extends while a custom trim remains fixed. ZIP manifests carry take/part identities, timing and real source gaps.\n  Closed parts carry measured encoded bounds and their own camera audio/video settings; shorter tails and older\n  single-file timeline gaps remain explicit. Source reuse for a different new recording remains a separate action. Design and verification evidence are in\n  `docs/recording-studio-monitoring-pause-append.md`.\n\n- Replaced the recording-detail modal with an authenticated preparation workspace at\n  `/admin/recording-studio/<recordingId>`, reusing the studio shell, browser lock, stable IDs and local media.\n  All camera, screen and audio sources now share a zoomable timeline, decoded thumbnails/sparse audio samples,\n  playhead and coordinated play/pause/seek/speed controls. Offset/segment mappings retain gaps and short sources;\n  playback waits for decoder starts, pausing/revealing a source settles its decoded frame, and decoder failures\n  hide stale frames and can be retried. Visual hide/solo and audio mute/solo only affect monitoring,\n  with one audible source initially; every source remains in exports. A common draggable IN/OUT range, precise\n  seconds, undo/reset and protected autosave persist a versioned recipe without changing original bytes. ZIP64\n  and individual-file exports preserve separate sources and embedded audio, include explicit source/session/export\n  timing, record video resampling to the source's nominal cadence, and validate transcoded boundaries within 50 ms\n  per component, including long final frames. Unsupported or discontinuous sources are\n  clearly labelled originals plus recipe. Cancellation/retry preserves originals; export holds the selected edit\n  steady and preserves incomplete trim drafts. Small individual prepared downloads survive temporary-file cleanup;\n  larger ones require direct disk saving instead of an unbounded memory copy. Legacy metadata and directory\n  checkpoints retain their IDs and saved selections, and deep links explain\n  absent local data. Added deterministic timecode/clap, late-session, failure/recovery and external FFmpeg checks;\n  verification details and unavailable macOS/physical-device tests are recorded in `docs/recording-studio-editor.md`.\n\n- Investigated the missing VS Code window reported on another macOS Space. The studio's shared capture path does not\n  enumerate or filter system windows; its optional `displaySurface` value is a type preference, and the browser/OS\n  owns the chooser. Added contextual Spaces guidance beside manual, restored, and historical screen-source selection,\n  plus an authenticated diagnostic which calls plain `getDisplayMedia({ video: true, audio: false })` and records the\n  browser's track events, selected surface, frame callbacks, permission/window-state details, and observed Space-switch\n  continuity. A muted required video track is now visibly unavailable, blocks Start, and interrupts an active take as\n  incomplete with reconnect guidance; an ended display source asks the administrator to select it again. Whole-display\n  sharing stays explicit and warns that other windows and notifications may be recorded. The investigation note\n  includes current standards/browser documentation, dated historical issue context, and a reproduction matrix. The\n  affected Mac/browser versions, system permission state, same-Space/fullscreen/minimized/hidden/monitor results, and\n  frame continuity are still unverified because the physical Mac was unavailable; neither the same-Space trial nor\n  whole-display continuation is claimed as a verified Space-switch workaround. `npm run test-types`, 31 focused unit\n  tests, and seven focused Playwright cases covering the plain probe, screen-source setup, cancellation, muted-source\n  handling, and restored/historic configurations passed. An earlier full 16-case run had one audio/video marker timing\n  assertion pass only on its automatic retry. Display picker/streams are synthetic and do not prove native macOS or\n  physical Windows picker behavior; a tested Space-switch workaround remains outstanding until the affected Mac is\n  reproduced.\n\n- Saved recordings now keep an immutable source-configuration snapshot, with **Použít tuto konfiguraci zdrojů** in\n  their list and editor. Reuse replaces a different browser setup only after confirmation, preserves matching live\n  previews, and routes remaining camera, microphone and display sources through the existing per-source reconnect\n  and readiness flow. Display sharing always requires the browser chooser again; no permission or stream is restored\n  from a saved window name, and reuse never starts recording or edits the original take. Legacy recordings recover\n  only stored track labels and audio details; unknown device identities stay unresolved until the administrator\n  chooses a device. Repeated reuse replaces cards instead of duplicating them.\n\n- Recording source setup now has a versioned schema migration for editable labels, stable logical IDs, order, enabled\n  sources, camera/microphone preferences, sound choices and preferred display-surface hints. Settings stay local to\n  this origin and browser profile, use the existing browser-storage layer, and contain no live streams, permission\n  grants or media. A completed or stopped take no longer releases healthy source previews; the cards say `Náhled\n  aktivní` until the administrator explicitly releases devices or leaves the page. Reload restores preferences but\n  never opens a camera, microphone or display chooser. Each source reconnects from its own action, saved display\n  choices remain hints for a newly opened browser chooser, and a readiness check blocks partial or unavailable takes.\n  The owner can label/reorder sources, disable a source, retry or replace a missing device, remove one source, or\n  explicitly reset the saved setup. Screen selection cancellation retains its setup, and an unavailable selected\n  camera/microphone is never silently replaced. Older source preferences and recording-directory manifests retain\n  their existing values through migration/defaults. All 64 recording-studio unit tests passed. The 12-case browser\n  suite passed in Playwright Chromium 151.0.7922.34 and Microsoft Edge 154.0.4258.37 on Windows 10 Pro 22H2\n  (10.0.19045.7663). Chromium needed its configured fresh-context retry once: the existing synthetic A/V marker\n  check measured 161 ms against its 150 ms bound on the first attempt, then passed on retry; Edge passed all cases\n  first attempt. Both suites closed and reopened the same persistent browser profile and verified that source cards\n  returned without camera, microphone or display capture calls. The added live-preview mute/unmute readiness case\n  also passed individually in both browsers; the full unit suite remained 64/64 after that change. E2E sources and\n  the display chooser are mocked, while MediaRecorder, browser storage, codecs and export remain real, so this\n  verifies browser lifecycle and recording paths rather than physical-device behavior. The reported macOS setup and\n  its native permissions were unavailable here; the owner's exact macOS and browser versions are also unknown.\n  Screen Capture requires renewed user activation and consent for every display request, so each reconnect opens the\n  browser chooser. A saved display-surface type is only a hint and is sent only when `getSupportedConstraints()`\n  reports it.\n\n- New camera sources now default to `Kamera + mikrofon`: choose a camera and a system-default or separate microphone,\n  with an explicit, enabled-by-default `Nahrávat zvuk` option. Camera and microphone are requested together and stored\n  in the same camera media file; the muted preview stays separate from the captured audio. Existing source intent is\n  retained in a versioned browser-local configuration, so a saved video-only choice stays silent and restored sources\n  require an explicit reconnect. The studio shows microphone identity, audio-track presence and a live level meter,\n  preserves a failed sound-enabled setup for retry or an explicit switch to silent video, and clones an already-open\n  matching microphone track safely when it is also configured as a standalone source. Recording metadata and archive\n  manifests now identify embedded camera audio and its selected microphone. Recorder containers and codecs are chosen\n  from combinations accepted by the active browser, with construction-time fallback; standalone audio remains separate.\n  Verification on Windows 10 Pro build 19045 used Playwright Chromium 151.0.7922.34 and Firefox 153.0: the full\n  Chromium recording-studio suite passed 9/9, the camera export contained audible audio, and 240 ms visual/audio\n  markers stayed within 150 ms at the beginning and end in both engines. Automated capture used generated canvas/audio\n  sources in place of physical devices; browser recording, playback, storage and export remained real. The permission UI\n  distinguishes denied, busy, and absent-device retries before an explicit silent-video choice. Chromium reported WebM VP9/Opus, WebM\n  VP8/Opus, generic WebM, and MP4 H.264/AAC candidates; Firefox reported WebM VP8/Opus and generic WebM, so the\n  recorder falls through to the first supported combination. The bundled Playwright WebKit 26.5 on Windows has no\n  `MediaRecorder` and disables the studio; this does not describe native Safari. The reported macOS device/browser\n  setup was not available in this workspace, so its hardware verification remains outstanding.\n\n- Quick-link materials now pass only the trimmed original pasted URL as their body to ordinary material creation,\n  preserving URL spelling, percent encoding, query strings and fragments. Scraped titles, fallback titles and title\n  corrections remain separate. The shared link extractor recognizes complete standalone URLs containing parentheses,\n  brackets or trailing punctuation, so existing tracking, preview cards and QR codes retain the full destination.\n  Previously saved content and the full Markdown editor are unchanged.\n\n- Added a compact email-only request form to the AI ta Krajta homepage. It records a dedicated podcast email-update\n  source and purpose note through the existing `/api/waitlist` contact pipeline, preserves the listener's email for\n  retry on failure, and confirms only after the contact write succeeds. The contacts source filter now includes every\n  source in a merged email history, keeping subscriber requests and collaboration inquiries independently filterable\n  and preserving both in exports. Privacy information links to its canonical Promptbook domain; no campaign sender was\n  added. The same form now appears in the shared podcast footer on the homepage, media kit and branding pages.\n\n- Fixed the AI ta Krajta snake's body wobbling at walls and corners. The simulation now keeps the path through each\n  reflected contact, and shared body strokes follow that path with width and colour tied to travelled distance.\n  The bounded trail stays stable through repeated steering toward an outside pointer and rescales with the canvas.\n  Added deterministic short- and grown-snake coverage for all walls, all corners, repeated rebounds, body joins and\n  responsive resizing.\n\n- Participant materials now show a compact preview card for every rendered link, with a safe page image, title, useful description, and destination domain when available. Each card flips to its existing `PromptbookQrCode` on request; only one QR face stays open in a material list, and its tracked short URL remains the same as the material's Markdown link and open action. Preview metadata loads lazily through an authenticated, visibility-checked room endpoint, which resolves stored shortcode destinations by read-only database lookup and reuses the shared public-page scraper and protected image loader. It neither visits click-tracked redirects nor creates links. Broken or unavailable previews leave the Markdown, open actions, and QR available; shared presentation and video cards use the same interaction.\n\n- Workshop material cards in `/admin/workshops?tab=content` now reorder from a dedicated mouse/touch drag handle or keyboard-accessible move controls and save automatically through the shared admin save queue. Focus stays with the moved material. The numeric order remains available under advanced editor options. A workshop-scoped database transaction locks and reindexes only material IDs, preserves content fields, reconciles concurrent additions and deletions, and broadcasts one room refresh after the complete order is committed.\n\n- Standardized admin editing around the existing shared autosave queue. Workshop materials, settings, polls, member\n  answers, chat corrections, agents, subtitles, contacts, discount codes, short links, and recording trims no longer\n  show a normal Save button; edit forms stay open and report waiting, saving, saved, validation, or request-failure\n  status, with retry only after a failure. Existing-record close actions are labelled clearly and flush before closing.\n  New workshop, material, poll, agent, subtitle, contact, discount-code, quick-link, short-link, and artificial-activity\n  drafts remain local until their explicit create action succeeds. Modified drafts now receive browser unload protection\n  and an explicit discard confirmation on controlled navigation, without turning close into creation. Material and\n  subtitle deletion settle pending edits first; workshop, poll, short-link, and discount-code deletions reject duplicate\n  requests while pending. Creation forms also guard repeated submissions. Validation errors have their own status and\n  do not offer a futile retry; failed requests retain a retry action. Dialog closes flush that editor's autosaves,\n  nested editors and active explicit operations. Discard prompts cover only drafts owned by that dialog and its nested\n  editors, so unrelated drafts do not block a clean close.\n  Workshop and discount-code creation fields lock during submission to preserve the submitted draft. Workshop settings\n  remain inline on their page.\n\n- Workshop settings now choose whether video, presentation, or the connected repository leads the stage. The choice\n  defaults to video, preserves every configured source, and follows the existing countdown, recorded-end, and wrap-up\n  phases. Other accessible sources stay in the shared special-material list exactly once; supplementary recordings\n  continue to use the server's member-aware video projection. Presentation and repository stage views reuse their\n  existing room components, and live settings saves use the existing room refresh broadcast.\n\n- Workshop and community participant administration now shows complete room-level counts for trusted people,\n  untrusted people, and moderators. **Důvěřovat všem** reviews the exact eligible room participants in a confirmation\n  dialog, then grants trust atomically only if that set is unchanged. The existing promotion trigger approves pending\n  submissions while preserving bans and rejected content. A separate, default-off setting can automatically trust only\n  newly created participant identities in that room; turning it off does not revoke earlier trust.\n\n- Workshop material administration now offers **Přidat materiál** for Markdown and **Přidat odkaz** for a quick\n  URL batch. Each valid, distinct URL becomes its own ordinary, editable material with a title from the shared safe\n  page preview or a clear domain fallback; the original query and fragment remain in its tracked link. The dialog\n  reports invalid, repeated and already used destinations, shows publication and access defaults, and creates only\n  on confirmation. Batches append after the largest stored material order, keep per-item failures for retry, and use\n  stable creation IDs to avoid duplicate records after a lost response. The existing short-link and live-room paths\n  handle every new material.\n\n- Isolated Promptbook, AI ta Krajta, and Pavol Hejný's Czech and English sites on the four configured\n  domains and their `www.` aliases within the existing deployment. Unknown, Promptbook-only, foreign-brand,\n  short-link, and unknown file-looking page paths on a branded domain now return that site's localized,\n  fully rendered HTTP 404 at the original URL. Legacy cross-site redirects still work from `ptbk.io`,\n  including podcast children, the `/pavol` language entry, trailing slashes and query strings.\n  Each site's robots file and sitemap describe only its own pages. Shared assets and contact APIs remain\n  available; admin pages stay outside the branded sites and admin APIs retain their authentication.\n  Updated personal language and project links, podcast profile and legal links to canonical destinations,\n  while same-site legal links stay on local and preview hosts. Added browser-level domain, status, metadata,\n  asset, API, and navigation coverage.\n\n- Configured the independently branded sites for their own canonical domains: AI ta Krajta now lives at\n  `https://ai-ta-krajta.cz/`, while Pavol Hejný's Czech and English pages live at\n  `https://pavolhejny.cz/` and `https://pavolhejny.com/`. One shared domain-route map rewrites those concise domain\n  roots to the existing app routes, permanently redirects the former `ptbk.io` paths (including podcast subpages),\n  preserves query strings, and keeps the custom domains' metadata, structured-data links, social cards, and sitemap\n  URLs canonical. Each branded site answers on both its bare apex and its `www.` alias, so a visitor who types\n  `www.ai-ta-krajta.cz`, `www.pavolhejny.cz`, or `www.pavolhejny.com` reaches the branded page instead of being\n  dropped onto the Promptbook homepage; `www.` is folded into the apex in one shared place for the primary and every\n  branded host alike. Shared build output, APIs and static files resolve on the branded host.\n\n- Added per-host episode-appearance factors to the `/ai-ta-krajta` roster draw. Hosts retain the ordinary 1×\n  contribution from their episode appearances, while Katka Fajmanová receives 1.7×, Tomáš Mikolov 5×, and Pavol Hejný\n  0.8× before weighted ordering.\n  The shared calculation affects both the hydration-safe initial order and each visitor's fresh randomized draw.\n\n- Added `Dneska` and `Zítra` event badges ahead of `Tento týden`, based on Prague calendar dates. Shared cards,\n  calendars, landing-page term choices, and the admin picker use the same phases and theme-aware colours. Terms\n  still switch to `Probíhá` at their start and remain eligible for waiting-room choices and follow-up recommendations.\n\n- Added the **Titulky** tab at `/admin/workshops?tab=subtitles` with private Czech, English and mixed-language tracks.\n  Admins can fetch available YouTube captions, generate timed subtitles from an uploaded video/audio recording,\n  import or edit SRT/WebVTT, and download either format. Long recordings are decoded in the browser and transcribed\n  in bounded audio chunks using the existing private OpenAI key; generated drafts are reviewed before explicit creation.\n  Existing tracks autosave through the shared editor, keep original-video timing and source information, and remain\n  separate from participant responses. Added a private subtitle-table migration and documented setup and limitations.\n\n- Workshop project previews on `/cs/komunita` and `/cs/online-workshop/participant` now share the first deployment's\n  image, title, description and address. Missing metadata or broken images retain the application's identity instead\n  of a generic GitHub preview; projects without a deployment keep the repository fallback. The participant preview\n  opens the deployed app alongside the existing repository and deployment links, and loads independently of chat and\n  commits. Late responses from previously selected rooms or projects are discarded; community cards still open the workshop.\n\n- Redesigned the workshop wrap-up PDF for sharing and A4 printing with the Promptbook logo, locally embedded\n  Inter/Outfit fonts, a light room palette, numbered sections and running headers/footers. It now includes a QR code\n  and readable ad hoc short link back to the workshop room, a project preview with all deployment links, and a\n  paginated vector Git graph using the same branch selection, commit bounds and lane layout as the materials panel.\n  Export preparation remains authenticated and uses the existing material-access projection; private room data is\n  excluded. External preview/history failures retain the recap and project links, and longer histories are labelled\n  with a link to continue in the room. No document is stored or workshop database field added.\n\n- Added `/admin/recording-studio` to the shared admin menu and dashboard. Multiple cameras, screen shares (with\n  available shared audio), and optional separate microphones start and stop together, with per-track sizes,\n  elapsed time, and an estimate of remaining browser storage time. Recording chunks persist locally in IndexedDB;\n  a source failure or storage limit stops the whole take, interrupted takes can be recovered, and a browser-wide\n  lock prevents another studio tab from changing an active recording. Saved recordings have shared autosaved\n  trimming and previews, explicit deletion, and ZIP64 downloads containing untouched source files and timing\n  metadata, optionally with separately trimmed copies for the editor. Large archives stream to disk where supported;\n  trimming runs locally using browser codecs and temporary files. Admin navigation waits for active recording and\n  export; reopening the studio waits for its previous instance to release local storage. No recording is uploaded\n  to the server.\n\n- Replaced inline admin creation and editing with shared, accessible popup dialogs across contacts, short links,\n  discount codes, workshop/community settings, materials, polls and member answers, chat corrections, Book agents,\n  artificial activity, and custom chart metrics. Lists now show summaries with explicit New/Edit actions; contact\n  notes and contacted status use the same contact editor. Dialogs contain request errors, keep long forms scrollable\n  on smaller screens, restore keyboard focus, and wait for autosave before closing while retaining invalid or failed drafts.\n\n- Added shared autosaving throughout `/admin` for existing workshop/community settings, materials, polls and answers,\n  chat corrections, Book agents, contacts, discount codes, and short links. Edits are debounced and saved in order;\n  background refreshes and older responses preserve newer typing. Pending or failed edits trigger the browser's\n  close/reload warning, while admin links, editor switches, and sign-out wait for saving. Validation and request\n  errors retain the draft with retry controls; new records and destructive actions keep their explicit buttons.\n  Immediate admin writes also protect the window while their requests are in progress.\n  Newer edits continue saving if an earlier request fails, incomplete discount dates stay protected, and contact\n  refreshes retain local changes. Unlocking materials uses their current draft; repeated poll saves preserve the\n  generated IDs and votes of newly added choices.\n\n- Added **Nasadit na Vercel** to project settings in `/admin/workshops` when a GitHub repository has no deployment URL.\n  The authenticated server integration imports the original repository, reuses one Vercel project per repository,\n  and deploys its production branch with future Git pushes connected. Administration shows progress and errors,\n  supports resuming status checks, and fills in the assigned production URL only after a successful build. The existing\n  settings save, validation, room links and previews handle the result; manual URLs and changed projects are preserved.\n  Documented private `VERCEL_TOKEN` / optional `VERCEL_TEAM_ID` setup; no database migration is needed.\n\n- Added independent starting and ending commit IDs to workshop project settings in `/admin/workshops`, with commit\n  message, author and date previews and separate date-based autofill buttons. The participant project graph opens on\n  the inclusive range and highlights it, with expansion and pagination for history outside it. Missing bounds leave\n  their respective side open. All views and lookups retain the selected branch patterns; unrelated branches stay\n  hidden. Commit IDs are validated and normalized on save, and the range is copied or cleared with its repository.\n  Concurrent autofill preserves both bounds, changing the branch selection discards pending history responses, and\n  temporary GitHub failures retain the loaded graph without announcing historical commits as new.\n\n- Granting trust or moderator status now approves all pending submissions by that room participant: chat messages,\n  custom poll answers (including shared polls), and community projects. Promotion and approval commit together;\n  rejected submissions stay rejected and interaction bans still block automatic approval. Moderators on\n  `/cs/online-workshop/participant` and `/cs/komunita`, and administrators in the participant list, see each author's\n  complete pending count. The shared project gallery refreshes with the room after approval.\n\n- Added light and dark modes to `/cs/komunita` and `/cs/online-workshop/participant`, including their waiting rooms\n  and shared project views. One accessible appearance control follows the device setting by default and remembers an\n  explicit choice across visits, tabs, and rooms. Shared palette tokens cover chat, polls, calendars, event cards,\n  materials and Markdown, project and membership dialogs, and cookie controls without duplicating the room UI.\n  Switching appearance preserves typed names, e-mails, chat drafts, and the connected session.\n\n- Allowed one isolated E2E retry for transient development-server or external-database failures. Each retry runs\n  the complete test with its original assertions; failed-attempt traces remain available for diagnosis.\n\n- Improved the shared event mini cards on `/cs/komunita`: removed star ratings and their unused feedback queries,\n  enlarged project previews with a wide image, readable title and description, and a repository fallback. Ended\n  workshops show a replay-length badge using the total video duration minus the configured recording start offset.\n  The calendar and card list use the same component and keep their existing destinations and participant hand-off.\n\n- Added a downloadable Czech wrap-up PDF to the ended stage of `/cs/online-workshop/participant?workshop=`.\n  It includes the workshop description, key points extracted from existing descriptions and materials, full readable\n  materials with clickable links, and any presentation, repository, and deployments. The download refreshes the\n  existing authenticated room state, preserving publication, unlock, and membership rules and refusing workshops\n  that have not ended or have been reopened. PDFs support Czech text and multiple pages and are generated in the\n  browser on demand, with no new administration, database fields, or saved documents.\n\n- Added a quiet display-settings switch to `/admin/workshops` and `/admin/community` for screen sharing. Artificial\n  controls stay hidden by default: prepared chat comments and reactions, synthetic viewer counts, and artificial\n  comment and poll-vote adjustments no longer appear among ordinary moderation controls. The switch is one compact\n  settings icon away and keeps its intentional state in the shareable address as `artopts=on` or `artopts=off`; it\n  changes no stored room data.\n\n- Added a fifth shared time state for event terms: a published term that begins within the next seven rolling days is\n  now marked `Tento týden`. The violet badge and calendar colour appear consistently in `/cs/komunita` and the term\n  picker of `/cs/online-workshop/participant?workshop=`, while `/admin/workshops` gives ongoing, freshly past,\n  next-seven-day, later upcoming, and historical terms their own ordered categories. The shared future-term helper\n  keeps these imminent terms eligible for the post-workshop recommendation too, so highlighting a near event never\n  makes it disappear as the next workshop.\n\n- Added reusable Book agents to workshop and community chat. The shared Agents tab in `/admin/workshops` and\n  `/admin/community` edits personalities with Promptbook `BookEditor`, enables each agent per room, and shows recent\n  activity. `LiteAgent` from `@promptbook/node` uses server-side `OPENAI_API_KEY` and each agent's source Book to reply\n  to approved participant, artificial and agent comments. A durable queue, per-agent cooldowns, leases and a two-turn\n  limit prevent duplicate replies and unbounded agent conversations. Replies use the existing chat, threads, links and\n  moderation; administration and CSV exports distinguish all three origins and retain agent/run identifiers.\n  Live workshops can share stream-tab audio or a presenter microphone from the Agents tab. Private rolling\n  transcripts supply timely questions; stopping capture, ending the event or disabling an agent prevents stale\n  questions. A restarted capture excludes previous sessions' speech, and publication locks the active session against\n  a concurrent stop. Books, transcripts and execution records remain private. Added migrations, isolated PostgreSQL tests,\n  browser-capture tests, and setup instructions in `README.md`.\n\n- Added follow-up actions to the ended stage of `/cs/online-workshop/participant?workshop=`:\n  non-paying attendees can buy membership through the existing popup even when no recording exists,\n  and everyone gets the next upcoming workshop, the next paid workshop, and an extra community button.\n  Recommendations use published future terms and the shared event cards; room links preserve the attendee's\n  identity. A term recommended in both roles appears once, and missing future terms show a short notice.\n  Replay, feedback, PDF and material access stay available.\n\n- Added a shared AI approval mechanism for chat in `/cs/online-workshop/participant?workshop=` and `/cs/komunita`,\n  member-written poll answers, community projects, and project discussions. New submissions are saved first, then\n  clearly suitable text can be approved automatically; uncertain content and unavailable AI stay in the existing\n  manual queue. Trusted members and moderators retain immediate approval, and banned authors cannot gain AI approval.\n  One atomic database operation protects concurrent human decisions, edits and deletions and privately records AI\n  approvals. The reviewer never rejects content or changes trust. Server configuration, the eight-second timeout,\n  provider setup, and the scope of text/URL review are documented in `README.md`; without a configured key, moderation\n  continues as before. Existing moderator-created materials need no approval and are outside the review queue.\n\n- Replaced the centered cookie popup on every page with a shallow desktop strip\n  and an inset mobile panel. The banner and its settings now use\n  light, workshop, or podcast colors together, with clearer button hierarchy,\n  keyboard focus, and scrollable settings on short screens. One shared measurement\n  hook keeps the banner, podcast player, coder badge, booking notice, and admin\n  table scrollbar clear of each other as they appear or resize; reserved space\n  keeps footer links reachable. Existing Czech/English copy, saved choices, and\n  the privacy page's cookie settings link remain available across all pages.\n\n- Put the answers members write into a community poll through the very same moderation a chat message goes through. An\n  `Other` answer written in `/cs/komunita` or in an attached `/cs/online-workshop/participant?workshop=` is no longer\n  public the moment it is written: it waits for a decision, while a trusted member and a moderator have theirs approved\n  as they write it, because a chat message, a shared project and now a poll answer are all decided by one shared\n  submission policy rather than by a rule each surface wrote for itself. The member who wrote the answer keeps seeing\n  it, marked `Čeká na schválení`, and their vote is counted for them straight away, so waiting for a moderator never\n  costs anybody their own choice; everybody else receives neither the answer nor its vote until it is approved, which\n  keeps a poll's total honest without a second counting rule. A rejected answer leaves the poll for everybody including\n  its writer, exactly as a rejected message leaves the chat. Deciding about an answer is offered where the decision\n  belongs: a moderator of the room which owns the poll approves or rejects it from the poll itself, by the same quiet\n  buttons which moderate a chat message, while a moderator of an occurrence the poll is merely about reads the same\n  answers every other member does, because a poll is administered by its community rather than by whichever room it is\n  attached to. `/admin/workshops` and `/admin/community` additionally say who wrote each answer, with the name and\n  normalized e-mail they connected with and the moment they wrote it, and can reword it, reject it, or remove it\n  together with the votes cast for it. A prepared choice of the administration is untouched by all of this: it is still\n  edited as part of its question, stays public, and is never attributed to a member. An answer written before this\n  change keeps being public, and its writer is recovered from the first vote it ever received, which is the vote the\n  writing itself cast.\n\n- Let an administrator write the start of a paid replay on a clock. The stage settings of `/admin/workshops` now ask\n  for `Začít záznam od` in its own `Hodiny`, `Minuty` and `Sekundy` boxes instead of in one number of seconds, so the\n  moment the workshop itself begins at is written as `0 : 1 : 15` rather than counted out as `75`. Nothing about the\n  offset itself changed: it is held, saved, exported and read by `/cs/online-workshop/participant?workshop=` in exactly\n  the same seconds as before, the field says underneath which number of seconds it is about to save, and a term which\n  was given its offset before this change opens on the very same position of its recording.\n\n- Let the project a term is about run in more than one place. The project settings of `/admin/workshops` now take one\n  address of a deployment per line instead of a single address altogether, and\n  `/cs/online-workshop/participant?workshop=` opens every one of them beside the repository the workshop follows. A\n  project deployed in one place is still simply its `Živá aplikace`, exactly as it was; several deployments are named\n  by the addresses they are reached at — `workshop.example/app` beside `staging.workshop.example/app` — because one\n  repeated name would say nothing about which of them a participant is opening. The compact card of the term in\n  `/cs/komunita` is previewed from the first written address, so a card still costs one request however many places\n  the project runs at, and the settings export writes them all on one line. Every deployment belongs to the connected\n  repository exactly as its branch patterns already did: they are written, changed and cleared as one connection, so\n  clearing the repository can leave behind no address of a project nobody is connected to. An address which cannot be\n  opened, and a second address which means the very same page, are refused when written and left out when read, while\n  an address stored before this change keeps its place as the first deployment of its project.\n\n- An administrator in `/admin/workshops` or a moderator in\n  `/cs/online-workshop/participant?workshop=` can now turn any chat comment into an immediately available material.\n  The source comment remains in the chat untouched; the new material keeps its complete Markdown body and names its\n  chat author in the title. Both entry points use the ordinary material-creation path, so its short links, live room\n  refresh, publication and member access behave exactly like a material created in the content editor.\n\n- Made the compact cards of the published terms in `/cs/komunita` tell more of the story of an event without giving\n  the calendar and the card-list two versions of it: the same card is shown below a selected calendar day, below a\n  month, and in the `Karty` view, and can now show the anonymous average of the star ratings with its count, a visual\n  preview of the project the workshop followed, and the real replay length. That length is the total public YouTube\n  duration less the start offset an administrator set to remove the waiting room, so `1:30:00` with a `75`-second\n  offset is named `1:28:45` rather than pretending the whole live stream is replay. Ratings are reduced before the\n  browser receives them — no response, author, or e-mail is published — and the raw recording identifier stays on the\n  server as well. A missing rating, project, deploy-preview, video, or public duration simply leaves that small part\n  off the card; the ordinary event link, calendar subscription, and membership gate keep exactly their former jobs.\n\n- A term which has only just been held is no longer one more term of the history. Where an event stands in time is now\n  one of four things instead of three — it is still ahead, it runs right now, it is freshly past while less than a day\n  has gone by since the end recorded for it, or it is past — and that is answered in the single place which already\n  answered the other three, so no list, badge, or colour can decide it on its own. In `/cs/komunita` such a term wears\n  its own amber `Právě proběhlo` badge, colours its own day of the calendar, is named in the legend beside the three\n  others, and is listed after what is ahead rather than at the head of the archive. In\n  `/cs/online-workshop/participant?workshop=` it is offered in the open under `Právě proběhlo`, between the workshops\n  which run or are coming and the `Proběhlé workshopy` disclosure, so somebody who was at last night's workshop finds\n  the room they have just left without unfolding the whole history to look for it. `/admin/workshops` lists such a term\n  under `Aktuální a nadcházející`, after what runs and what is coming, because the workshop of last night is the one an\n  administrator is still working on — reading its participants, moderating its comments, publishing its recording — and\n  its `Historie` now holds only the terms nobody is wrapping up any more, so opening a freshly held term no longer\n  unfolds that archive either. Everything which opens only after a workshop is over is untouched: the wrap-up, its PDF,\n  the feedback, and the paid recording all read a freshly past term as exactly as finished as one from last spring.\n\n- A term near enough to be looked forward to is now named rather than merely dated. One held today reads\n  `dnes, úterý 15. 9. 2026 · 11:11`, one held tomorrow `zítra, středa 16. 9. 2026 · 11:11`, and one held later in the\n  same week `tento čtvrtek 17. 9. 2026 · 11:11` — in the gender the name of that weekday has in Czech, so that\n  `tento čtvrtek` stands beside `tato středa` and `toto úterý`. A week runs from Monday to Sunday, as it does in the\n  Czech Republic, and a term further away than that stays the plain date it always was, so a list of distant terms\n  does not grow a weekday it never showed. The waiting room and the term picker of `/cs/online-workshop/participant`,\n  the cards and the calendar day of `/cs/komunita`, the header, hero, term picker and chosen-term line of\n  `/cs/online-workshop`, its thank-you page, and the term picker of `/ai-supervize-mini` all say it, because how near a\n  day is is worked out once, from the day a term falls on in Prague and the day the page was built on. That day comes\n  from the server rather than from the browser, so a page says exactly what it was sent as instead of renaming its\n  terms the instant it hydrates. Nothing which is not a term read against today changed: the times of chat messages and\n  materials, the dates a membership is paid to, the printed participant sheet, the published calendar, and the notes a\n  registration is counted by are untouched.\n\n- Moved the community polls attached to an occurrence to the bottom of `/cs/online-workshop/participant?workshop=`.\n  A participant now reads the stage, the invitation, and everything the workshop hands over in its materials first, and\n  is asked for their vote below them, because a poll a workshop is merely the subject of matters less to its\n  participant than the materials they came for.
